Nigma's ultra-late-game style (57-min average wins, 7 of 8 wins >45 min) makes them dangerous in extended fights but vulnerable to Falcons' stronger early-game (Falcons +993 gold @10 in wins). Falcons' 0-3 record when trailing 2k+ at 15 min is a concern against Nigma's comeback style, but their superior early tempo and higher skill ceiling give them a modest edge. H2H favors Falcons 2-0 from pre-TI BO1s. Overall a close series with Falcons slight favorites.

Falcons hold a ~60-point Elo advantage, 2-0 H2H record, and superior early-game metrics (+376 gold at 10 min vs Nigma's -212), making them deserved favorites. However, Nigma's TI form is exceptional (4W-1L, 8-2 maps, sweeping LGD/Vici/Team Spirit 2-0), their late-game grind style (54-min avg, 7 wins >45 min) neutralizes Falcons' early edge in extended series, and Falcons have shown vulnerability (losses to Iron Wing, TEAM VISION; 0-3 when trailing 2k+ at 15 min). Falcons' ban priorities (Ember Spirit, Largo) target Nigma's best heroes, but Nigma's momentum and confidence after a 0-4-to-top-3 turnaround give them a genuine ~38% shot—slightly above the 33.3% implied by the 3.00 price.

Nigma Galaxy’s 8-2 TI map record and four consecutive 2-0 wins provide strong momentum, but Falcons retain the Elo edge, stronger early-game metrics, deeper event sample, and two recent H2H map wins. Falcons are a narrow favorite, with Nigma’s late-game resilience making a close series likely and Falcons’ recent victories mostly coming 2-1.

Falcons' higher Elo, stronger early-game profile, and 2-0 recent H2H keep them a modest favorite, but Nigma's 8-2 TI map run, four straight sweeps, and equal rest narrow the gap substantially. Falcons have been more prone to deciding maps while Nigma's wins have all been sweeps, making 1:2 the modal score and leaving Nigma's underdog prices attractive.

Falcons retain a narrow baseline edge from their 60-point Elo advantage, two recent H2H map wins, and substantially better event gold/XP trajectories through 30 minutes. Nigma's 8-2 TI map record after the opening loss, four straight sweeps, flexible Ember/NP drafting, and demonstrated late-game recoveries make an extended close series plausible rather than a decisive Falcons edge.

Falcons' Elo, pre-event form, and recent H2H edge make them a modest favorite, but Nigma's 8-2 TI map record—including four consecutive 2:0 wins—and proven late-game resilience sharply narrow the gap. Falcons playing five three-map series in six at TI supports a close-series distribution.

Falcons have the stronger baseline through higher Elo, better pre-event form, two recent BO1 H2H wins, and positive early-to-midgame differentials; their Ember Spirit and Largo bans also target two of Nigma's strongest event picks. Nigma's 8-2 map run and four consecutive sweeps keep this close, but many wins required long recoveries from deficits, a less reliable route against Falcons. With equal rest, Falcons are modest favorites, most likely in three maps.

Falcons remain slight-to-moderate favorites due to their Elo edge, cleaner early-to-midgame differentials, larger sample of tested drafts and two recent H2H map wins. Nigma's 8-2 TI run with four consecutive sweeps materially narrows the gap, but its reliance on long comebacks is vulnerable if Falcons convert their usual leads.

Falcons hold higher Elo, stronger pre-TI form (7-5 vs NGX 3-9), and recent H2H dominance, but NGX's strong TI run (4-1, 8-2 maps) and underdog narrative from flipping 0-4 to top-3 provide balance, resulting in near-even series odds.

Nigma Galaxy is on a strong TI 2026 run with four straight 2-0 wins against top teams, showcasing strong form despite poor pre-event results. Team Falcons have higher Elo and recent H2H wins over Nigma but show inconsistency (4-2 at event, poor pre-TI form). This leads to a competitive BO3 where Nigma's momentum gives them a 45% series win probability, higher than the market implies.

Team Falcons enter as the reigning champions with superior Elo, proven LAN consistency, and a 2-0 recent H2H advantage over Nigma Galaxy. While Nigma have shown impressive late-game resilience and momentum at TI with an 8-2 map record, their persistent early deficits (-2.2k gold @20min) leave them vulnerable against Falcons' disciplined mid-game snowballing and hero pool depth.

While Team Falcons hold a historical Elo edge and won their prior H2H, Nigma Galaxy have displayed exceptional form at this TI with four consecutive 2-0 sweeps over top contenders. Falcons have looked vulnerable, dropping maps in five of their six tournament matches, making Nigma's true win probability significantly higher than implied by the 3.00 market price.

Falcons hold the higher Elo and won both recent H2H meetings, but Nigma enters with the better TI form (8-2 maps, four straight 2-0 sweeps) and a proven late-game comeback style, while Falcons have been more vulnerable in longer games. I give Nigma roughly a 36% series win probability, slightly above the 33.3% implied by the 3.00 moneyline.

Nigma Galaxy enters on a hot streak (4 consecutive 2:0 sweeps in group stage, including a dominant win over Team Spirit), but with a newly reshuffled roster (SumaiL and lorenof joined in June 2026). Team Falcons are the defending TI 2025 champions with the same stable core since November 2023 (skiter, Malr1ne, ATF, Cr1t-, Sneyking), giving them a playoff pedigree and synergy edge. Falcons' group stage was less clean (4-2) with two 1:2 losses, but they closed with a 2:0 vs Vici. In a best-of-3 upper bracket matchup between two strong teams, I lean slightly toward Falcons due to championship experience and roster stability, though Nigma's current form makes it close. Expecting a likely three-game series.

Nigma Galaxy enters the Upper Bracket on a hot streak: four consecutive 2:0 sweeps (OG, LGD, Vici, Spirit) after an opening 0:2 to Iron Wing, with their rebuilt SumaiL/lorenof lineup peaking on 7.41e and comfortable in the Ember/Hoodwink/Clockwerk meta. Team Falcons are the defending TI champions with a stable skiter/Malr1ne/ATF/Cr1t-/Sneyking core and strong pedigree, but at this TI they have been shakier — three 2:1 grinds and two series losses (TEAM VISION, Iron Wing) — though they can flatten teams (2:0 over Vici). Common opponents are a wash (both took Vici 2:0; Nigma beat LGD 2:0 vs Falcons' 2:1). This gives Nigma a narrow edge in a competitive series, but Falcons' ability to take maps and end sweeps keeps the 2:0 Nigma outcome from being dominant.

Nigma Galaxy finished Group A 4-1 (8-2 maps, 80% game WR) and qualified directly to the upper bracket, riding an 8-map win streak that includes 2:0 over Team Spirit and LGD Gaming. Falcons went 3-2 (8-7 maps, 53% game WR) and needed an elimination-round 2:0 over Vici, though they faced a meaningfully harder schedule (opponent game WR ~55.7% vs Nigma's ~44.3%), lost only to unbeaten TEAM VISION and to Iron Wing (which also beat Nigma), and have won four straight series. No direct H2H this tournament and no roster issues. Nigma is a moderate favorite on form and seeding, but Falcons' pedigree and tougher path keep the gap modest.

Nigma Galaxy were one of the strongest group-stage teams (4-1, 8-2 maps, 80% GW), riding a four-series 2:0 streak including wins over LGD, Vici and a strong Team Spirit; their only loss was 0:2 to Iron Wing. Team Falcons went 3-2 (7-7 maps) with narrow 2:1 wins and needed the elimination round, losing to TEAM VISION and Iron Wing. Common-opponent comparison favors Nigma (2:0 vs LGD where Falcons went 2:1), and Nigma's cores (23, 精神~) are posting dominant KDA/GPM numbers on meta heroes like Ember Spirit and Nature's Prophet. Falcons are resilient and rarely get swept, so a 2:1 is live, but Nigma are clear favorites. I estimate ~60% per-map edge for Nigma, giving ~65% series win probability.

Nigma Galaxy enter on a dominant 4-series win streak, sweeping OG, LGD, Vici and top contender Team Spirit (including a 43-23 dismantling); even their tight maps (LGD 43-42, Spirit 59-61 min) ended in wins, showing consistent late-game execution. Team Falcons are 4-2 with two losses to mid-tier sides (a 94-min marathon vs TEAM VISION and a 46-13 map collapse to Iron Wing) and most wins came via deciders, including an 8-40 blowout loss to BoomBoys in a series they still won 2:1 — high skill but poor consistency. No head-to-head exists at this event. Quality and consistency of form clearly favor Nigma, so I model ~0.59 per-map win probability for Nigma in this BO3.

Nigma Galaxy enter on a hot streak: four straight 2-0 sweeps (OG, LGD, Vici, Team Spirit), 8-2 in maps, their only loss a Day-1 blowout to Iron Wing that they have clearly moved past. Falcons (higher long-term pedigree, world top-5 core) have been shakier at this event: 4-2 in series but 9-7 in maps, dropping series to TEAM VISION and Iron Wing and needing deciders vs LGD, GamerLegion and BoomBoys, though they crushed Vici. Common-opponent comparisons (both swept Vici; Nigma swept LGD while Falcons dropped a game; Iron Wing beat both) lean slightly Nigma's way. Falcons have taken a map in every series they've lost here, so their losses would more likely be 1-2 than 0-2; Nigma's current form suggests they can also close 2-0.

Nigma Galaxy enter with the stronger tournament profile: a 4-1 group record, 8-2 map score, direct upper-bracket qualification, and four consecutive 2-0 series wins. Their recent drafts have successfully centered on high-impact Ember, Clockwerk, Windranger and Nature’s Prophet cores, while Falcons’ Sven, Pangolier, Lina and Clockwerk compositions remain dangerous and their championship roster gives them strong BO3 resilience. There is no tournament head-to-head; Falcons’ 3-2 group record and 8-7 map score, followed by a 2-0 elimination win, make this competitive but give Nigma a modest edge.

Nigma reached playoffs directly at 4-1 with an 8-2 map record, posting four straight 2-0s after its opening loss and capping them against Team Spirit; Falcons went 3-2 (8-7) in groups and required a 2-0 Vici elimination-round win. Nigma's demonstrated Ember/NP core setup fits its current form, but Falcons retain the unchanged 2025 championship five and Aui_2000's BO3 preparation, keeping the form-based Nigma edge narrow; there is no tournament head-to-head.

Nigma has the sharper TI form at 4-1 in series and 8-2 in maps, with four consecutive 2-0 wins including Team Spirit, effective draft flexes and resilient late-game execution. Falcons faced a stronger schedule, then swept Vici, retain their intact TI 2025 championship roster and defeated this Nigma lineup 2-0 shortly before TI; that matchup evidence and playoff pedigree make Falcons a narrow favorite despite Nigma's momentum. No tournament H2H or stand-in issue is evident.

Nigma Galaxy showed strong form with 4-1 record, winning 3 straight 2-0 series before a 0-2 loss, indicating good momentum and map control. Team Falcons had 4-2 record with 3-1 in last 4 series, including 2-1 wins, showing competitiveness but less consistency. No prior H2H at TI, but both are top-tier with similar recent play; Nigma edges out on draft flexibility and recent wins against strong teams like Spirit. Patch 7.41e favors aggressive playstyles, but Falcons' veteran experience may counter. Expect close series, Nigma favored to win 2-1 or 2-0 in upper bracket quarterfinals.

Nigma Galaxy enter the Upper Bracket playoffs on an eight-game win streak, having swept OG, LGD, Vici Gaming, and Team Spirit 2-0 to qualify with a 4-1 Swiss record. Defending TI champions Team Falcons navigated a turbulent Swiss stage where all five series went to three maps before finding their rhythm with a 2-0 elimination round sweep over Vici Gaming. While Falcons possess top-tier stage pedigree and strategic depth, Nigma Galaxy's surging momentum and drafting synergy around SumaiL and lorenof give them a narrow edge in a highly competitive clash.

Nigma Galaxy enter the UB quarterfinal in clearly stronger form: after an opening 0-2 loss to Iron Wing they reeled off four straight 2-0 sweeps (OG, LGD, Vici, Team Spirit), showing deep drafting flexibility on Ember/Hoodwink/Timbersaw/Clinkz and strong farm distribution. Team Falcons went 4-2 but needed three maps to get past LGD, GamerLegion and BoomBoys, and lost series to TEAM VISION and Iron Wing; they often drop the first map before recovering behind Sneyking's tempo drafts and fast-push Clinkz/Pangolier. No head-to-head at this event, so I weight current form and map-level dominance: roughly 0.59 per-map edge for Nigma, translating to ~0.63 series win with Falcons' scrappiness keeping 2-1 and 1-2 outcomes live.

Nigma Galaxy enters with a hot 4-series win streak (all 2-0 vs OG, LGD, Vici, Team Spirit) at TI2026, with a rebuilt roster (SumaiL-lorenof-Davai-OmaR-GH) showing great chemistry. Their only loss was a 0-2 to Iron Wing. Team Falcons (TI2025 defending champions) had a slower group stage, losing 1-2 to TEAM VISION and 1-2 to Iron Wing before recovering with three straight wins (2-1, 2-1, 2-0). Falcons' roster is more experienced in high-pressure matches but showed real vulnerability. In a BO3 playoff, I give Falcons a slight edge due to TI experience, but Nigma's form is undervalued. The bookmaker's 1.45 on Falcons overstates their chances; Nigma ML at 3.00 offers value.

Nigma enter hot: 3rd in Swiss (above Falcons' 6th) with an 8-0 map run, including a 2:0 over Team Spirit and a cleaner 2:0 over LGD than Falcons' 2:1. Falcons remain the reigning TI champions with the same five + Aui_2000, but their Swiss was shakier (1:2 losses to TEAM VISION and Iron Wing, multiple game-3s), and the same Iron Wing 2:0'd Nigma on day one. Market consensus prices Nigma ~33%; my form-weighted estimate gives Nigma roughly 38% to win the series, slightly above the implied price, while Falcons stay favored overall.

Nigma finished the Swiss group 4-1 as the #3 seed with four consecutive 2:0 sweeps (including Team Spirit), while Falcons went 3-2 with losses to TEAM VISION and Iron Wing and dropped maps to weaker GamerLegion/BoomBoys before qualifying via the elimination round. Falcons still hold the pedigree edge (star-studded roster, Aui_2000, 4-1 season H2H, harder schedule at TI), so I keep them as moderate favorites (~60%), but the market price of 1.45/3.00 overvalues reputation versus current form. Nigma ML at 3.00 and Nigma -1.5 at 6.30 both offer value given Nigma's sweep-heavy win pattern (all four TI wins 2:0).

Nigma arrives on 4 straight 2:0 sweeps (OG, LGD, Vici, Team Spirit — Spirit then swept Iron Wing in playoffs), while Falcons are erratic: 1:2 losses to TEAM VISION and Iron Wing plus three tight 2:1 wins. Both teams are at full strength; Falcons are the star-laden reigning TI champions, but an independent main-event power ranking put Nigma #2 and Falcons #6 among the final 8, and Nigma's in-tournament form and grind-style draft execution look superior. The 3.00/1.45 book line looks anchored to Falcons' reputation, so my estimate gives Nigma a modest edge with real value on Nigma ML and Nigma -1.5.

Nigma Galaxy enter on a four-series hot streak, all 2:0 (OG, LGD, Vici, and a dominant 2:0 over Team Spirit, 43-23 kills in game two), while defending champions Team Falcons have been shaky at this event: three 2:1 wins plus series losses to TEAM VISION and Iron Wing (including a 46-13 map stomp), going 10-7 on maps vs Nigma's 8-2. Common-opponent comparisons (LGD, Vici, Iron Wing) slightly favor Nigma, and pre-event power rankings also ranked Nigma above Falcons; Falcons' pedigree and playoff experience keep them competitive, but at ~53% per-map for Nigma the market's 1.45 on Falcons looks like reputation pricing.

Nigma Galaxy enter the UB QF on a dominant run: four consecutive 2:0 sweeps, including a decisive 43-23 win over elite Team Spirit, with their only blemish an early 0:2 to Iron Wing. Falcons are 4-2 with mostly narrow 2:1 wins and two group losses (Vision, Iron Wing), showing less dominance. The market overrates Falcons' reputation relative to current form, underpricing Nigma's ML and sweep line even though Nigma projects as roughly a 42% series winner.

Nigma's 4-1 group record and 8-2 map score, including four straight sweeps over OG, LGD, Vici and Spirit, show stronger current form than Falcons' 3-2 group record and 8-7 map score, though Falcons added a 2-0 elimination-round win over Vici. Falcons' unchanged TI-winning roster and high-ceiling Clinkz, Lina and Pangolier cores keep them a narrow favorite, while Nigma's flexible Nature's Prophet, Ember Spirit, Windranger and Clockwerk drafts give them meaningful upset and sweep potential; there is no tournament H2H or reported stand-in.
Nigma won 2:0 vs OG (good), but lost 0:2 to Iron Wing (bad). Falcons went 2:1 vs LGD, lost 1:2 to Vision (both close), 2:0 vs Vici. Falcons favored in BO3 here.

Team Falcons enter the series as the defending TI champions with exceptional tactical depth under coach Aui_2000, but their Swiss stage campaign was turbulent, dropping maps in five of their six series. Conversely, Nigma Galaxy have been the standout surprise of the tournament, riding an eight-map winning streak after clean 2:0 victories over top contenders including Team Spirit, Vici Gaming, and LGD. With SumaiL and lorenof exhibiting peak carry form and versatile mid-game execution, the market heavily underestimates Nigma's competitive chances against a vulnerable Falcons lineup.

Nigma earned the direct playoff berth at 4-1 with an 8-2 map record, capped by a 2-0 over Spirit; their repeated Ember/Nature's Prophet core structures have fitted the 7.41e field well. Falcons retain the stronger long-term, title-winning core, but their 3-2 Swiss run was volatile, with series losses to both Team Vision and Iron Wing before the Vici sweep. I keep Falcons as a modest favorite rather than the market's heavy one.

Nigma enter on an eight-map winning streak, including 2:0 victories over LGD, Vici and Spirit, although several wins were long and closely contested. Falcons remain favored due to their unchanged championship roster, superior draft depth and playoff experience, but their 10-7 tournament map record and repeated dropped maps make the matchup closer than the moneyline suggests; there is no tournament H2H.

Swiss form favors Nigma (4-1, 80% game WR, four straight 2:0s incl. Spirit) vs Falcons (3-2, 53% GW, 2-1 wins over mid teams and a 0:2-in-maps-level loss to Iron Wing); schedule-strength adjustment (Nigma OGW 44% vs Falcons 56%) narrows the gap, and both were 2-2/4-5 in maps vs playoff-caliber sides, leaving Nigma a modest ~54% per-map edge (~56% series). Pundit rankings (Nigma #2, Falcons #6) corroborate this, while betboom's 1.48/3.00 line looks anchored on Falcons' brand, so Nigma ML and Nigma -1.5 carry value.

BoomBoys hold a clear Elo edge (1392 vs 1277, ~114 points, ~64% base), plus a 3-1 all-time H2H advantage and 2-1 at this TI. However, Iron Wing have been the more in-form team at TI itself (4W-3L, 10-8 maps) versus BoomBoys (3W-4L, 8-9), with a notable comeback narrative versus this same opponent. BoomBoys' phase metrics are heavily negative (gold diff -3267 at 30min in losses), and Kataomi himself admitted throwing late leads. This suggests BB's wins tend to be grindy and they can falter when closing — so I expect fewer BB 2:0 sweeps than raw Elo implies. Net assessment: slight BoomBoys favorite (~55%) with reasonable chance of an Iron Wing map regardless. 2-0 sweeps are less likely for BB given their throw-tendency; IW's decisive wins profile (gold diff +8151 at 30min in wins) makes a 2:0 IW also plausible.

BoomBoys hold a meaningful Elo advantage (1392 vs 1278, ~115 points), a 3-1 recent H2H lead including 2-1 at this event, and clearly better pre-event form (7W-5L vs 4W-8L). Iron Wing has higher variance and demonstrated comeback ability (record TI comeback vs BoomBoys), so series should go to 3 games frequently, but BoomBoys' structural advantages make them modest favorites. Iron Wing's 'all-or-nothing' profile (huge gold swings in both wins and losses) plus BoomBoys' late-game 'throwing leads' tendency support a close-to-coin-flip with BB slight edge. BoomBoys at 1.80 offers thin but positive value vs my ~59% true probability; the other lines are overpriced against my estimates.

BoomBoys enter as the slight favorite via higher Elo and winning the prior H2H series 2-1, but Iron Wing has shown better recent tournament form and BoomBoys have a recurring pattern of letting leads slip. Both teams play long, grinding maps, so a 2-1 split is the most likely single outcome; Iron Wing's chances mostly come through close games rather than a clean sweep.

BoomBoys have the higher Elo and an early-event H2H edge, but Iron Wing have looked better since that group-stage meeting: 3-2 in their next five series with positive gold/XP differentials, while BoomBoys are 2-4 and have repeatedly thrown leads. IW's draft priorities also take away BB's key Ember/Undying/Lina options, making BB's slow-comeback style fragile in an elimination BO3. I set IW's per-map win rate at 47%, giving them a series win probability just above 45%.

BoomBoys have a clear Elo and head-to-head advantage, but Iron Wing's better recent TI map record and BoomBoys' tendency to throw late-game leads narrow the gap. I estimate Iron Wing as roughly a 42% favorite per map, making BoomBoys a modest series favorite in this elimination match.

BoomBoys hold a 114-point Elo advantage, a 3-1 recent map edge over Iron Wing, and a top ban priority that targets Iron Wing's best event hero, Earth Spirit. Iron Wing's TI map form and strong phase stats keep it close, but I rate the per-map split around 45/55 in BoomBoys' favor, producing a roughly 57.5% series win probability.

Elo (~114 pts) and recent H2H (3-1 BoomBoys, incl. 2:1 at this event) favor BoomBoys, but Iron Wing's tag-Elo understates an ex-Tundra core that is 4W-3L at TI with clearly better phase stats (+300/+1243/+3005 gold vs BB's -381/-940/-3267 and a 0:43 first-blood avg vs 2:05). BoomBoys carry a recurring 'throwing leads' theme (lost the record-comeback game to IW, threw deciders vs Vision) and rely on late comebacks, while IW has draft answers (Undying/Lina/Ember/Winter Wyvern bans) even if BoomBoys deletes Earth Spirit. I make it roughly 55/45 BoomBoys with a high decider rate given both teams' long game times and 2:1-heavy series histories.

Despite BoomBoys' Elo edge (1392 vs 1278) and the 2:1 H2H win on Aug 13, event data favors Iron Wing: better series record (4-3 vs 3-4), strongly positive economy (+3005 gold @30min vs -3267), an ex-Tundra core whose Elo likely understates its true level, and a decider in that H2H where IW was in position to win. BoomBoys show a chronic late-game discipline problem ('throwing leads' vs Vision and IW), negative gold diffs even in wins, and 4 losses in their last 6. Both teams are decider-prone (~50% of their series go to game 3), so I model a heavy 2:1/1:2 distribution with IW ~55% to take the series — far above the 43.5% implied by their 2.30 price.

Elo (1392 vs 1278) and H2H (BoomBoys 3-1 in recent series, including a 2:1 win at this event on Aug 13) favor BoomBoys, but Iron Wing's event form is arguably better: 4-3 series vs 3-4, and Iron Wing posts positive gold/XP differentials at every timestamp while BoomBoys are negative across the board and survive on comebacks. Iron Wing's Elo is depressed by a pre-event slump and understates the ex-Tundra core's pedigree, so I shade this much closer than raw Elo (~66%) suggests. BoomBoys' recurring 'thrown leads' theme (vs Vision twice and the record comeback loss to Iron Wing) plus Iron Wing's stronger late-game economy stats keep the upset very live, but BoomBoys' targeted Earth Spirit bans (removing Iron Wing's best flex, 6W-1L) and their H2H edge make them modest favorites. Both sides are equally rested off Aug 20 losses. I land on BoomBoys ~58% to win the series.

Elo favors BoomBoys (1392 vs 1278) and they won the group-stage H2H 2:1, but Iron Wing's rating reflects a rebranded ex-Tundra roster that won four Tier-1 titles this season and is underperforming its talent. At this event Iron Wing owns clearly superior phase stats (+1243 gold @20 vs BB's -940), a better series record (4-3 vs 3-4), and the H2H decider was a toss-up in which IW held a winning position; BoomBoys shows a recurring pattern of throwing leads (record comeback loss vs IW, thrown decider vs Vision) and went 1-4 in their last five series. I rate this near a coin flip with a slight Iron Wing lean (~52%), making the 2.30 on IW ML (implied ~43.5%) a solid value; the handicaps offer no edge (IW -1.5 needs a 2:0 I price at 17% vs 22.7% implied, and BB +1.5 at 1.23 is priced fair against my 83%).

BoomBoys hold a clear Elo advantage (1392 vs 1278) and won the group-stage BO3 2-1, with all-time H2H 3-1 in series. Iron Wing's early-game metrics are stronger but they dropped their last match; both teams are on equal rest. Given BoomBoys' slight edge and tendency for split maps, we favor BoomBoys to win the series ~62%, with Iron Wing's wins more likely 2-1 than 2-0.

BoomBoys possess higher Elo (1392 vs 1278) and won the group-stage BO3 2-1, though both teams are inconsistent and Iron Wing shows strong early-game metrics. Independent model assigns Iron Wing ~0.42 single-game win probability, resulting in series score probabilities that favor BoomBoys winning the series and usually not by 2-0.

BoomBoys holds a clear Elo advantage (~115 points) and leads the H2H 3-1 including a 2-1 series win at this TI. However, BoomBoys' 3-4 TI record, negative phase stats, and well-documented tendency to throw leads (admitted by Kataomi, evidenced by the record comeback Iron Wing staged in their group-stage meeting) narrow the gap. Iron Wing's positive gold/XP trajectory and ability to grind long games give them a genuine path, but BoomBoys' higher individual skill ceiling and proven success in this matchup make them moderate favorites in an elimination BO3.

BoomBoys hold a meaningful Elo advantage (~115 points) and won the TI group-stage H2H 2-1, but that series was extremely close with Iron Wing nearly completing a record comeback in game 3. At TI, Iron Wing's series record (4-3) edges BoomBoys (3-4), and IW's statistical profile (positive gold diffs scaling to +3005 at 30min) is notably stronger than BB's (negative diffs throughout). However, BoomBoys' higher individual skill ceilings (gpk~ 4-0 on Ember/Snapfire, Kiritych~ superior carry GPM) and greater overall experience give them the edge in a must-win BO3. Iron Wing's 0-4 on Ember Spirit and vulnerability to BB's draft targeting of Earth Spirit (banned 12 times) slightly tilt the draft phase to BoomBoys. I land on roughly 37-63 in BoomBoys' favour, with a high probability of the series going to three games given the H2H history.

BoomBoys' substantial Elo/rank edge, better pre-event record, and 3-1 all-time H2H make them the favorite, reinforced by their recent 2-1 win over Iron Wing. Iron Wing's stronger TI map and economy profile, intact decorated core, and BoomBoys' documented late-game discipline issues keep the matchup close and make a deciding map likely; both teams' zero-rest load adds uncertainty.

BoomBoys have the stronger baseline from the Elo gap, higher global standing, and favorable recent head-to-head, while Iron Wing's better TI map record and recent comeback history make this competitive. With equal rest and both teams coming off close losses, BoomBoys remain a modest series favorite, with a low sweep rate expected.

BoomBoys have the stronger Elo, pre-event form, and 3-1 all-time H2H edge, including their 2-1 TI win. Iron Wing’s 4-3 TI record, 10-8 map record, and substantially stronger average economy trends offset much of that advantage, while BoomBoys' documented lead-conversion issues make this a close elimination series. I retain a narrow BoomBoys edge based on the broader rating, form, and matchup evidence.

Iron Wing's 10-8 TI map record and substantially stronger 10/20/30-minute economy offset much of BoomBoys' Elo and 2-1 event head-to-head edge; BoomBoys' recurring difficulty converting leads further narrows the matchup. The prior three-game meeting and both teams' long-game profiles make a decider more likely than either sweep, leaving BoomBoys a narrow series favorite.

Iron Wing has a narrow edge from its stronger TI map record and substantially better event economy and phase metrics. BoomBoys' higher Elo, 3-1 map H2H, recent 2-1 win in this matchup, and frequent Earth Spirit bans keep the series close, while both teams' inconsistent lead conversion favors a three-map outcome.

BoomBoys retain the Elo and recent H2H advantages, and their Earth Spirit bans directly attack Iron Wing's strongest flex pick. However, Iron Wing's better TI map record and substantially stronger early-to-mid-game economy metrics make this close to even, while BoomBoys' recurring issues converting leads add upset potential.

BoomBoys hold higher Elo (1392 vs 1278), superior event H2H (2:1), and stronger pre-event form (7-5 vs 4-8). Iron Wing shows talent but inconsistency and draft issues (Earth Spirit bans). Close series expected but BB slight favorite.

Iron Wing and BoomBoys show similar recent event records (IW 4-3, BB 3-4 series) but BB holds the higher Elo rating and won their prior H2H encounter 2-1. Draft contests favor BB with bans on Earth Spirit (IW's top flex pick), though IW's positive gold/XP diffs in wins provide balance. Overall slight edge to BB based on metrics and history, but Iron Wing's win-form edge keeps the series close.

BoomBoys enters as slight favorites backed by a higher Elo rating (1392 vs 1278) and a 2-1 head-to-head victory over Iron Wing earlier in the group stage. Although Iron Wing boasts superior macro gold differentials and a decorated veteran core, BoomBoys' drafting and late-game resilience give them the edge in a tightly contested series likely to go the full three maps.

While BoomBoys won their group-stage meeting 2-1 and hold a higher Elo rating, Iron Wing possess significantly superior in-game metrics at this tournament (+3005 gold diff @30min vs BoomBoys' -3267). BoomBoys have consistently struggled to close out late-game leads, making this series a near-even contest where Iron Wing at 2.30 ML represents substantial betting value.

Close matchup in the lower bracket. H2H favors BoomBoys (2:1 win on 2026-08-13), which gives them a slight edge. Iron Wing has a marginally better overall W-L record at TI (4-3 vs 3-4) including a strong win over Team Falcons, but lost 0:2 to Team Spirit in their most recent outing. BoomBoys enters after a 1:2 loss to TEAM VISION but has shown they can beat mid-tier opponents convincingly. Both teams have shown similar patterns - 2:1 series are common, 0:2 sweeps are less frequent. The H2H advantage and slightly more stable drafting give BoomBoys a marginal edge in this rematch.

Lower-bracket elimination between two similarly-tiered teams. Iron Wing (1w) has the better tournament record (4-3) with quality wins over Falcons, GamerLegion, Yandex and Nigma, losing only to top teams (Liquid, Spirit). BoomBoys (BetBoom) is 3-4 with an 0:2 and 1:2 to TEAM VISION and a 1:2 to Falcons, and their deciding game vs Vision was a 31-min blowout. The only H2H was a close 2:1 BoomBoys win decided in a 69-min game 3, but Iron Wing dominated its won map 36-11. Marginal edge to Iron Wing, with high likelihood of a three-map series given both squads' tendency to split close games.

Both are elite CIS rosters meeting in an elimination BO3: Iron Wing (the transferred Tundra lineup of Pure, bzm, 33, Ari, Whitemon) went 3-2 in Swiss with strong wins over Nigma 2:0 and Falcons 2:1, while BoomBoys (BetBoom's Kiritych, gpk, MieRo, Save-, Kataomi) went 2-3 but won the direct head-to-head 2:1 on day one, eliminated Aurora 2:0, and pushed #1 seed TEAM VISION to three games in the upper-bracket quarterfinal. Iron Wing were swept by Spirit (one stomp, one 62-min loss), BoomBoys fell 1:2 to VISION. Form, strength of schedule and pedigree slightly favor Iron Wing, but the H2H win and BoomBoys' competitiveness against the top seed keep it close, so I price Iron Wing a modest favorite per map (~0.53) and for the series (~0.55).

Both teams fell to LB R1 via UB quarterfinal losses, but the competitive evidence favors Iron Wing modestly: they went 4-3 in the Swiss stage with wins over Falcons, Yandex, GamerLegion and Nigma, and their losses came only against elite sides (Liquid in 3, a Spirit sweep), while BoomBoys went 3-4 with wins only over OG, Iron Wing and Aurora, losing twice to TEAM VISION and collapsing 8-32 in a 31-minute decider map on Aug 20. BoomBoys did win the only H2H 2-1 (Aug 13) in a genuinely close series, and their Kez/Lina-centric drafts fit the meta, so the edge is small. I put Iron Wing around 57% for the series with 2:0 slightly more likely than 2:1 given both teams' swingy, stomp-prone map profiles.

BoomBoys won the only H2H (2:1 in groups) behind star carry Sage of the Six Paths, which likely drives their 1.80 favorite status, but Iron Wing's overall TI resume is clearly stronger: 2:0 over Nigma Galaxy and 2:1 over Team Yandex (both upper-bracket semifinalists), plus wins over Falcons and GamerLegion, 10-8 in maps, with the only bad loss being 0:2 to title contender Spirit. BoomBoys are 1W-4L since beating Iron Wing, swept 0:2 three times and crushed 8:32 in their last decider map, though their ceiling stays high via their carry. The H2H series was swingy on both sides (all three maps were one-sided), so I weight sweeps more than a typical BO3. My Iron Wing series probability (~0.54) is well above the 0.435 implied by the 2.30 ML price, creating value there and on the -1.5 handicap.

Iron Wing (4W-3L) and BoomBoys (3W-4L) are closely matched. IW has stronger wins (2-1 over Falcons/Yandex, 2-0 over Nigma/GL), while BoomBoys' losses include two 0-2 sweeps to TEAM VISION. H2H was a close 2-1 to BoomBoys, but market is overrating BoomBoys given IW's quality wins and better series record. IW's sweep tendency (3 of 4 wins are 2-0) makes the -1.5 line appealing. Model gives BoomBoys slight edge (52%) due to H2H but finds value in Iron Wing prices.

Iron Wing are the ex-Tundra core (33, Pure, bzm) competing under a new banner, 4-3 in the TI group stage with quality wins (Falcons 2:1, GL 2:0) and tight losses only to top sides (Liquid 1:2, Spirit 0:2). BoomBoys (BetBoom) beat Iron Wing 2:1 in groups via a 69-min Drow outscale, but have been shakier overall (0:2 Aurora, two losses to TEAM VISION, including an 8-32 stomp in their last map). The market prices BoomBoys ~55.6% (1.80) and Iron Wing ~43.5% (2.30); I see the gap smaller, roughly 53/47 toward BoomBoys, giving modest value on the Iron Wing ML.

Near coin-flip rematch of BoomBoys' razor-thin earlier 2:1 win (two 50+ min grinds + a 69-min decider). Iron Wing shows steadier form (0-2 only to elite Spirit; clean sweeps of mid-tier) while BoomBoys are erratic (twice swept by TEAM VISION, once by Aurora). I rate Iron Wing a hair better than the market's 43.5% implied, so Iron Wing ML at 2.30 carries value; long close games cap the sweep probability on both sides.

Both teams dropped from UB quarterfinals on Aug 20 (Iron Wing 0:2 Spirit, BoomBoys 1:2 VISION). Iron Wing's tournament body of work is stronger: 4W-3L series (10-8 maps) with wins over current UB semifinalists Nigma and Yandex plus Falcons (who beat BoomBoys), their losses coming only vs BoomBoys (1:2, 69-min decider), Liquid and Spirit. BoomBoys went 3W-4L (8-9 maps), lost twice to VISION and once to Falcons, but hold the direct H2H 2:1 from Aug 13 where all maps were competitive. Rosters are stable on both sides. Slight edge to Iron Wing on overall form and opposition-adjusted results, but the H2H and BoomBoys' late-game resilience (Sage's Kez/Drow) keep it close; both teams' series frequently go to a decider, so a 3-map series is the most likely outcome.

Near-even matchup: BoomBoys edged the group-stage H2H 2:1 but game 3 was a 69-minute coin flip, and since then Iron Wing has been clearly stronger (beat Falcons/Yandex/GamerLegion, losses only to Liquid and Spirit) while BoomBoys went 2-3 with two losses to VISION and one to Falcons. Tournament map win rate slightly favors Iron Wing (9-9 vs 8-10). I rate Iron Wing a small favorite (~53%), so their ML at 2.30 (implied 43.5%) and the 2:0 at 4.40 (implied 22.7%) carry positive expected value; BoomBoys-side prices offer none.

Both teams are mid-pack at TI2026 and are coming off losses into the Lower Bracket (Iron Wing dropped 0-2 to Team Spirit, BoomBoys lost 1-2 to TEAM VISION). Recent form is similar (Iron Wing 4-3, BoomBoys 3-4) but BoomBoys hold the only head-to-head, a 2-1 win on 2026-08-13. With BoomBoys slightly favored on H2H and comparable form, I model Iron Wing's per-map win probability at ~0.46, making this a near coin-flip BO3 tilted marginally to BoomBoys.

BoomBoys won the group-stage H2H 2-1, but Iron Wing hold the stronger tournament resume (wins over Falcons, Yandex, GamerLegion, Nigma; forgivable sweep by title favorite Team Spirit), while BoomBoys are wildly volatile with two 0-2 losses and only narrow three-game defeats recently. Iron Wing's Arianka on low-winrate Hoodwink is an exploitable weakness, but overall form and scalps give Iron Wing a slight edge in this close, likely three-game series.

H2H is 1:2 to BoomBoys (Aug 13, close series; Iron Wing won its map 36-11). Since then form diverged sharply: Iron Wing went 3-2 with wins over Falcons, Yandex and GamerLegions (only losing to top-tier Liquid and Spirit), while BoomBoys went 1-4 with two losses to VISION and losses to Aurora/Falcons. Both lost their Aug-20 openers (IW 0-2 to Spirit, BB 1-2 to VISION). Iron Wing's trajectory and quality of wins suggest improvement and a slight edge, despite the market pricing BoomBoys as favorite on the early H2H. I estimate Iron Wing map win ~0.52, a coinflip-leaning series.

Iron Wing's cached run is marginally stronger (4-3 in series, 10-8 in maps) than BoomBoys' 3-4, 8-9, and Iron also played two maps rather than BoomBoys' three in the latest elimination loss. BoomBoys won the only H2H 2-1, but that meeting was highly draft-sensitive: their Kez/Drow/Largo cores took two games while Iron Wing's Doom/Tiny/Kez setup took the middle game; both teams otherwise have access to the high-value Kez/Ember pool, while Iron's repeated Hoodwink is a lower-win tournament staple. Stable lineups in the cached games reduce roster uncertainty, so I make Iron Wing only a narrow favorite and expect a deciding map.

These teams met in the group stage on Aug 13, with BoomBoys winning 2-1 in a close series (decider went 69 minutes). Since then, Iron Wing have been the stronger side: 3-1 in series with wins over Team Falcons, Team Yandex and GamerLegion, and losses only to Team Liquid and the champion-caliber Team Spirit. BoomBoys are 1-3 since that H2H, including two 0-2 sweeps by TEAM VISION and Aurora and a 1-2 rematch loss to TEAM VISION on Aug 20, while Iron Wing's Aug 20 loss (0-2) came against tournament favorite Spirit. Map differential also favors Iron Wing (+2 vs -2). No standin news found for either roster. I make this essentially a coinflip with a slight edge to in-form Iron Wing, so BoomBoys at 1.80 (implied ~56%) looks overpriced and Iron Wing at 2.30 offers value.

Iron Wing owns the better TI series record (4-3 versus 3-4) and showed draft adaptability in its 2-1 win over Yandex, including a deciding-map win after Kez and Hoodwink were banned. BoomBoys did win the August 13 head-to-head 2-1, and its Drow/Puck/Largo-oriented comfort drafts remain a meaningful matchup threat. Both teams arrive after upper-bracket losses, so Iron Wing is only a narrow favorite in a series with substantial three-map potential.

Iron Wing are 4-3 in their last seven series and have beaten Falcons and swept GamerLegion, while BoomBoys are 3-4; the only head-to-head was BoomBoys' narrow 2-1. Both appear to be using established tournament lineups, and Iron's Kez, Earth Spirit, and Undying options fit the meta, although BoomBoys' flexible cores and that head-to-head keep them a slight favorite after their respective August 20 losses.

Iron Wing have the stronger overall tournament record at 4-3 in series and 10-8 in maps, with notable wins over Falcons, Yandex and Nigma, while BoomBoys are 3-4 and 8-9. Iron Wing have shown a slightly better fit with high-performing 7.41e heroes such as Earth Spirit, Kez and Necrophos, but BoomBoys won the only head-to-head 2-1 and demonstrated the stronger late-game execution in that matchup. With both teams fielding stable lineups, Iron Wing hold a narrow edge, while a three-map series is most likely.

Iron Wing went 4-2 in groups with a 10-6 map record and beat Falcons 2-1, better event form than BoomBoys' 3-3/7-7. However, BoomBoys won their direct 2-1, kept Largo away from Iron in all three maps, and can target Iron's Hoodwink-heavy approach, leaving BoomBoys only a marginal edge and a decider as the likeliest shape.

Iron Wing has the stronger tournament body of work at 10-8 in maps, including wins over Nigma, Falcons and Yandex, while BoomBoys is 8-9. BoomBoys' prior 2-1 head-to-head win, proven lineup and map taken from TEAM VISION keep this close, with a three-map series more likely than a sweep.

Iron Wing has strong playoff form after sweeping GamerLegion, while BoomBoys advanced similarly. No direct matchup history in this tournament. Under patch 7.41e and in lower bracket, Iron Wing holds a slight edge in roster quality and draft flexibility, making them favorites in a best-of-3 series.

Iron Wing and BoomBoys are evenly matched CIS contenders who previously fought a 3-map thriller in the group stage. While BoomBoys won that initial head-to-head 2:1, Iron Wing has exhibited better consistency across the tournament with victories over top opponents like Team Falcons, Team Yandex, and Nigma Galaxy. With both teams heavily contested on signature comfort picks like Kez, Doom, and Hoodwink, another protracted, closely fought series going to three maps is highly probable, with a marginal edge to Iron Wing's recent form.

Iron Wing is a lower-tier Russian squad (rank ~22) that had a disappointing group stage but showed form by sweeping GamerLegion to reach playoffs; they lack top-tier experience. BoomBoys (BetBoom, rank ~7) are more consistent, having eliminated Aurora and are a stronger side with better overall results. In this lower bracket R1, BoomBoys are favorites (~1.8 ML implied ~0.55). My estimates give BoomBoys ~62% win series outright, favoring 2:0/2:1 over 1:2/0:2. No strong value on ML as odds too close to my prob; handicap -1.5 for Iron Wing has edge.

Iron Wing (Pure, bzm, 33, Ari, Whitemon) and BoomBoys (BetBoom Team) are evenly matched, as demonstrated by their razor-thin 3-map group clash. However, Iron Wing has displayed higher overall form and draft versatility across the tournament with victories over Falcons and Yandex, while 33's playoff drafting offers tactical advantages. The market heavily prices BoomBoys as favorites, creating substantial value on Iron Wing ML and the -1.5 handicap.

Team Liquid enters as the moderate favorite. They hold a higher Elo (1427 vs 1384), a 3-2 series lead in the H2H, and notably swept Falcons 3-0 in the 1win Essence II grand final just ~2 weeks before TI. Liquid's roster features multiple TI winners (miCKe, Nisha, Boxi) chasing a 2nd Aegis, while Falcons' defending-champion core has publicly acknowledged the roster is breaking up after TI, with only one 2025-26 title to show. Falcons are also poor at closing from behind (0 wins when trailing 5k+ @15min) and play long, indecisive games (49 min avg). However, Liquid just got swept 0-2 by Yandex, their early-game gold/XP differentials are negative, and Falcons have shown they can grind out BO3 wins at this event. Calibrating to roughly a 60-40 series edge to Liquid, with a meaningful chance of a sweep either way.

Team Liquid holds meaningful edges in Elo (+43), pre-event series form (9-3 vs 7-5), and crucially just swept Falcons 3-0 in the 1win Essence II grand final ~2 weeks ago. Falcons as defending champs have experience, but their roster is publicly breaking up after this TI (morale factor), they've lost 3 of their last 4 series, and Liquid's drafting toolkit (targeted bans on Doom/Undying/Lifestealer/Hoodwink) effectively denies Falcons' comfort picks. Liquid also finished as the higher group seed (2nd) while Falcons had to climb through the lower bracket. Calibrating to ~60% Liquid series win probability; their early-game weakness (-174 gold @10min) makes 2:0 less likely than 2:1, so I weight the more competitive score paths slightly higher than a flat split.

Liquid enters with the higher Elo, stronger recent tournament form, and a decisive 3-0 grand-final sweep over Falcons just before TI; their contested draft heroes and hero-pool flexibility also give them a real edge. Falcons remain a veteran, defensively stubborn roster that can force long, messy maps, so I still give them a meaningful chance to take the series, but Liquid is the clear favorite. My score probabilities are built around roughly a 60% Liquid map-win rate in this matchup.

Liquid holds the Elo edge, won the last three direct meetings including a grand-final sweep at 1win Essence II, and has posted comparable if not better TI map quality. Falcons remain dangerous but their Dire-side struggles and longer-game tendency make a 2-0 more likely for Liquid than the market implies. I model Liquid near a 60% series win probability, with a solid 2-0 share at 32%.

Liquid are moderate favorites: they hold an Elo edge (1427 vs 1384), stronger pre-event form, and swept Falcons 3-0 in their most recent meeting at 1win Essence II. Falcons counter with defending-champ experience and solid draft options (e.g. Clockwerk, Pangolier), so the BO3 stays competitive.

Liquid's better Elo, most recent H2H form (including a 3-0 grand-final sweep over Falcons), and stronger overall tournament record give them a small but meaningful edge. Falcons have superior early-game gold/XP trends and dangerous individual play, but their long average losses and latest 1-2 defeat reduce confidence. I rate Liquid about 56-57% per map, producing a 60% series win probability.

Liquid hold edges in Elo (1427 vs 1384), pre-TI form (9W-3L with a 3-0 grand final sweep of Falcons at 1win Essence II) and TI form (4W-2L vs 4W-3L), while Falcons' late loss to Nigma and roster-breakup noise temper their defending-champion pedigree. Counterpoints: Falcons start games better (avg +176 gold @10 vs Liquid's -174), Liquid has shown no comeback ability when trailing 2k+ @15 (0/4), and Falcons' grind-long style (49min avg) plus Liquid's frequent 2:1 results suggest many maps stay close. I price Liquid ~62% for the series with a per-map edge near 0.59, moderately favoring a 2:0 given Liquid's superior peak form and H2H momentum.

Liquid hold a ~43-point Elo edge, better pre-event form, and a 3-0 grand-final sweep of Falcons two weeks ago, but their 0-2 collapse to Yandex and weak early-game numbers at this TI (-174 gold @10min) against Falcons' positive tempo (+176 @10min) keep this closer than raw ratings suggest. Both teams' TI map records are nearly identical (56% vs 55%) and neither has won from 2k+ down, so games are correlated and sweeps are less likely than an independence model implies; I make Liquid ~57.5% for the series with 2:1 the modal score. Only Liquid ML at 1.85 (implied 0.54) beats my number; the handicap prices offer no value.

Liquid enter as moderate favorites: +43 Elo (#8 vs #22 globally), a dominant 3-0 sweep of Falcons in the 1win Essence II grand final two weeks ago, and a stronger TI run (2nd seed group stage, wins over Vici/Yandex/Iron Wing/Aurora) against a tougher schedule than Falcons faced. Falcons counter with better early-game metrics (+532 gold @20 vs Liquid's -342; +136 GPM/map edge) and have been stubbornly competitive — all three TI losses were 1-2, never swept — while Liquid dropped a map in three of their four TI wins, suggesting a close series is likely. Liquid's late-game superiority (+528 @30, strong comeback profile vs Falcons' 0-for-4 when trailing) and draft edges on contested heroes (Windranger, Hoodwink) tilt a decider their way. Both teams are rested equally; Falcons' impending roster split and mixed 2026 season add mild uncertainty. I land near 59% Liquid series win with 2:1 the modal scoreline given Falcons' consistent map-stealing.

Liquid hold the clearer edge: higher Elo (#8 vs #22), a 3-0 sweep of Falcons in the 1win Essence II final two weeks ago, stronger pre-event form (9W-3L with a title), and a better group stage (2nd seed, 4-1) while Falcons needed the elimination round and carry roster-split distractions as defending champs with a mixed season. Falcons' superior event gold differentials are inflated by weaker elimination-round opposition (BoomBoys, GamerLegion), and Liquid's losses came against top sides (Spirit, Yandex). I put Liquid at ~60% to win the series, with a 2:0 slightly more likely than any single losing scoreline; that makes their ML at 1.85 (implied 54%) and the -1.5 handicap at 3.30 (implied 30.3%) modest value, while Falcons' lines are fairly priced or worse.

Liquid holds Elo and recent H2H edge (swept Falcons 3-0 in last event final) with stable roster; Falcons are defending champs but show split rumours and mixed form. Both teams frequently play 3-map series, so Liquid favored ~0.60 to win, with 2-1 most likely.

Liquid hold Elo and recent H2H edge (3-2 in last meetings, swept Essence II final), though both lost previous series; draft matchups favor Liquid's Windranger/Hoodwink. Model gives Liquid ~59% series win, with 2:0 around 32%.

Liquid enters as the stronger side: higher Elo (1427 vs 1384), better pre-event form (9-3 vs 7-5), and a dominant 3-0 sweep of Falcons in the 1win Essence II grand final just two weeks ago. Nisha and m1CKe are in excellent individual form, and Liquid's late-game scaling (positive gold diff at 30 min) suits the longer TI games. Falcons have defending-champion pedigree, 700+ maps of roster continuity, and a slightly stronger early game, but their Dire-side win rate (43%) is a vulnerability, and the confirmed post-TI roster split may weigh on focus. Both teams lost their most recent TI series (Liquid 0-2 to Yandex, Falcons 1-2 to Nigma), so neither carries momentum into this elimination match. Overall Liquid's draft flexibility, recent H2H dominance, and superior mid-to-late game teamfight give them roughly a 60% series edge.

Liquid hold a modest Elo edge (+43) and swept Falcons 3-0 in the 1win Essence II grand final two weeks ago, giving them psychological momentum. However, Falcons' superior phase stats (positive gold at all time-points vs Liquid's slow starts), defending-champion experience, and deeper event sample (20 vs 16 maps) keep this competitive. Both teams enter off losses (Liquid 0-2 to Yandex, Falcons 1-2 to Nigma), adding variance. Liquid's targeted bans on Undying/Doom hit Falcons' support pool, while Falcons' KotL/Treant/Ember bans blunt Liquid's flex options. I see Liquid as a ~56% favourite in a series most likely decided 2-1 either way.

Team Liquid is a modest favorite on higher Elo, stronger pre-event form, and the recent 3-0 H2H, while Falcons' defending-champion experience and stronger event-level economy keep the matchup competitive. Both teams have no rest and are coming off losses, so a three-map series is more likely than a one-sided result.

Liquid has the stronger Elo, better recent series profile and a recent 3-0 over Falcons, while equal rest and Falcons' TI experience keep the matchup close; I therefore make Liquid a modest favorite with 2-1 the most likely score.

Liquid’s Elo, superior pre-event and TI series results, and recent 3-0 Essence II grand-final win over Falcons establish a modest edge. Falcons’ stronger aggregate event 20-minute gold/XP numbers, useful Pangolier and Clockwerk options, and equal rest temper that advantage, so a three-map series remains most likely.

Liquid hold a modest edge through the 42.8 Elo advantage, a 4-2 TI record versus Falcons' 4-3, and their recent 3-0 Essence II grand-final win over Falcons. Equal rest and Falcons' stronger event-average midgame economy limit that edge, while both sides' TI results suggest a competitive three-map series is plausible.

Liquid are a modest favorite based on their higher Elo, stronger pre-event form, and the 3-0 Essence II final win over Falcons. Falcons' better average early-to-midgame differentials at TI keep the matchup competitive, while both teams' frequent three-map series make 2:1 the likeliest result.

Liquid has the stronger baseline through its higher Elo, better pre-event form, slightly better TI series record, and most recent 3-0 result against Falcons. Falcons' superior event phase differentials and ability to extend games narrow the gap, making Liquid only a moderate favorite with a three-map series slightly more likely than a sweep.

Team Liquid is the favorite with a higher Elo rating, stronger pre-TI form (9-3 maps), and a recent 3-0 sweep over Falcons. Falcons as defending champs with strong players are competitive but the BO3 should favor Liquid in this elimination matchup.

Liquid holds a clear edge via higher Elo (1427 vs 1384), stronger pre-TI form (9-3 series), and 3-0 H2H sweep vs Falcons pre-event. Falcons show roster fatigue signals but remain competitive with strong TI recent wins. Liquid leads in contested picks (Windranger/Hoodwink) and phase metrics (gold/XP diffs). BO3 variance exists but series win prob for Liquid exceeds 65%.

Team Liquid holds an Elo advantage and recently swept Team Falcons 3-0 in the grand finals of 1win Essence II just prior to TI. While Falcons possess championship pedigree, their form throughout the group stage and early playoffs has been inconsistent compared to Liquid's solid baseline.

Team Liquid holds a clear Elo and head-to-head advantage, having swept Team Falcons 3-0 in the grand final of 1win Essence II right before TI. Falcons have shown vulnerability throughout the tournament with losses to TEAM VISION, Iron Wing, and Nigma Galaxy, whereas Liquid secured direct playoff qualification with a 4-1 group stage run. Liquid's draft flexibility around Windranger and Hoodwink counters Falcons' narrower comfort pools.

Elimination BO3 between two evenly matched teams that both fell in the UB quarterfinals. Liquid's event résumé is cleaner: their only losses came to UB semifinalists (Spirit, Yandex), they beat Yandex 2:1 in groups, and they comfortably dispatched Iron Wing — the very team that beat Falcons — while Falcons dropped series to Iron Wing, TEAM VISION and Nigma. Falcons were more competitive in their Aug 20 loss (dominant map 1, 60-min decider) than Liquid, who were stomped 0:2 by a red-hot Yandex, which tempers Liquid's edge. Both teams play many three-map series (Liquid 9-7, Falcons 11-9 in maps), so I model a slight Liquid advantage (~55% per map) with a modest draft-adaptation tilt, giving roughly 57/43.

Team Liquid enters with a stronger group-stage performance (4-1, 64.3% GW) than Falcons (3-2, 53.3% GW) and a slightly better series record at the event (4-2 vs 4-3). Most importantly, Liquid swept Falcons 2-0 in the pre-tournament 1win Essence II final, giving them a clear stylistic and psychological edge. However, both teams lost their upper-bracket matches one day prior (Liquid 0-2 to Yandex, Falcons 1-2 to Nigma), and both are running heavily reworked lineups (Liquid with three stand-ins beyond tOfu/Boxi; Falcons with four players new since TI 2025). Falcons has a strong, stable carry in 'I m Going To Be 10k Player' and showed fight by taking a map off Nigma, keeping this close to a coin-flip. Slight Liquid edge overall; expect a competitive BO3 most likely to go three maps.

Liquid finished 2nd in the Swiss stage (Falcons 6th) and won their only two common-opponent checks (2:0 over Vici like Falcons, but 2:1 over Iron Wing whom Falcons lost to 1:2), with stronger top-8 wins (Iron Wing, Aurora). However, Liquid just got swept 0:2 by a red-hot Yandex in the UB quarterfinal, while Falcons' losses were all competitive 1:2s to top teams (VISION, Iron Wing, Nigma) and they won their elimination-round match dominantly. Net: a near coin-flip with a slight edge to Liquid's higher-quality tournament résumé, tempered by Falcons' better recent form and momentum.

Both teams enter LB R1 after UB defeats and are highly even: Liquid is 4-2 (9-7 maps), Falcons 4-3 (11-9 maps), no H2H at the event, similar map rates. Falcons look slightly more stable: they were competitive in their most recent loss to Nigma (won map 1, close decider), were never swept at this TI, and have dominant swing wins, while Liquid's fresh 0-2 to Yandex included a 38-minute blowout suggesting a lower floor. Liquid's three 2-1 comeback wins keep this close, but Falcons hold a modest edge.

Both teams come off losses in the lower bracket - Liquid was swept 0:2 by Team Yandex (map 2 was a 13-38 stomp), while Falcons lost 1:2 to Nigma Galaxy (won map 1 decisively, lost map 2 badly, dropped a close map 3). Over the tournament window, Liquid is 4-2 and Falcons 4-3, with similar profiles of inconsistency. Falcons have shown more 2:1 series (high variance), while Liquid have shown they can also drop series 1:2. Falcons' 2:0 win over Vici shows they can close cleanly, but so did Liquid's 2:0 over Vici earlier. Overall I see this as roughly coin-flip with a small edge to Liquid based on their cleaner series wins when they win, and the fact that bookmakers are pricing Liquid as a slight favorite. Probability of Liquid ML ~0.56, Falcons ~0.44.

Near-even elimination BO3 with a slight Liquid lean: better TI group record (4W-2L incl. wins over Yandex/Aurora/Iron Wing and a shared-opponent edge over Falcons), and a 3-0 BO5 sweep of Falcons two weeks before TI. Falcons are the defending champs with a higher ceiling (won map 1 vs Nigma 25:8) but are volatile and 1:2 in most recent series; both teams just lost in the UB QF. With nearly every recent series going 3 maps, expect a close multi-map series.

Both teams enter LB R1 off UB quarterfinal losses with similar overall form (Liquid 4-2, Falcons 4-3 in groups). Liquid's resume is slightly better (beat Yandex and Iron Wing; Falcons lost to Iron Wing and repeatedly dropped maps to mid-tier teams), while Falcons bring TI champion pedigree, a stronger game-1 record (5-2 vs Liquid's 2-4), and a closer playoff exit (1:2 vs Nigma vs Liquid's 0:2). Net: near coin-flip with a small Liquid edge (~0.51-0.52 series win). Both squads are heavily game-3 prone (10 of 13 combined series went the distance), so I weight 2:1/1:2 outcomes well above sweeps; after margin, none of the offered prices beat my fair probabilities, so no value bets.
