TEAM VISION (=PARIVISION, world #1, 16-win streak, 5-0 at TI) swept Team Spirit 2:0 in their Aug 15 H2H including a 7:37 kill demolition, and both of Spirit's TI losses were 0:2 sweeps — a clear matchup edge. Spirit only rebounded against weaker sides (Resilience 2:1, Iron Wing 2:0) after swapping in black reaper at carry. I estimate VISION ~0.67 to win; their ML implied prob (0.645) offers thin value, while the other lines do not clear their implied odds.

TEAM VISION's 5-0 tournament run, recent 2:0 head-to-head sweep, stable Satanic/Noone/Noticed/9Class/Dukalis roster, and strong Earth Spirit-centered meta fit make them the deserved favorite. Team Spirit's 5-2 form, wins over Liquid and Aurora, elite Yatoro/Larl/Collapse core, and ability to adapt its drafts give it more upset equity than the market implies; I expect a competitive series rather than a clear sweep.

TEAM VISION is 5-0 at TI (10-3 maps) after a 4-0 group, and its 2-0 over Spirit six days ago included a 65-24 aggregate kill margin; Satanic's scaling cores and Vision's Earth Spirit execution fit the 7.41e event pool. Spirit's Liquid win and fresh Iron Wing sweep supply enough recovery and decider upside to avoid calling a rout, but Vision's steadier form and direct draft edge make it the clear favorite.

TEAM VISION has the stronger tournament profile: a 5-0 series record, 10-3 map record, top Swiss seed and a decisive 2-0 head-to-head win over Spirit. Satanic and No[o]ne have excelled in the 7.41e core meta, while VISION also showed draft resilience when Earth Spirit was banned throughout its playoff opener. Spirit's recent sweep and strong Yatoro-Larl form preserve meaningful upset potential.

TEAM VISION dominated the only prior meeting (2:0 win in group stage). Spirit showed form with recent 2:0 wins but lost both games to VISION. VISION has 5W-0L in recent series, strong roster fit for current meta (Hoodwink, Earth Spirit high pick rates). No major draft news or rosters changes noted. Spirit ML odds imply ~27% win prob, but H2H edge and recent form give VISION slight series edge.

TEAM VISION enters the Upper Bracket Semifinals undefeated at TI 2026 (5-0 series record), including a convincing 2:0 victory over Team Spirit during the group stage. While Team Spirit displayed great playoff form by sweeping Iron Wing 2:0, TEAM VISION's carry pacing and drafting flexibility give them the upper hand. A competitive series leaning towards TEAM VISION (especially 2:1 or 2:0) is expected, with current market pricing fairly aligned with fair value.

TEAM VISION swept this exact opponent 2:0 in the group stage and is 5-0 in series at TI2026, with carry Satanic (a former Spirit sub) and Have fun on Earth Spirit in elite form. Spirit looked strong in a 2:0 playoff win over Iron Wing and did swap in a new core ('black reaper') after the H2H loss, which slightly reduces the head-to-head's predictive weight, but Spirit's two same-day 0:2 collapses and VISION's unbroken series record make VISION a clear favorite. My estimate of ~63% for VISION matches the market, leaving no value in any listed price.

TEAM VISION is 5-0 at TI2026 with the top Swiss seed and already beat Spirit 2:0 in the group stage, with Satanic in dominant form; Spirit went 3-2 in Swiss but owns wins over Liquid and a strong Iron Wing (ex-Tundra) squad and brings its two-time TI champion core (Yatoro/Larl/Collapse). I rate VISION the favorite at roughly 60% per map, giving Spirit about a 39% series chance — slightly above what the 2.70 moneyline implies — while VISION's most likely winning score is a clean 2:0 given their map dominance in the H2H.

TEAM VISION (PARIVISION) enter unbeaten at 5-0 and dismantled Team Spirit 0:2 just six days ago (37-7 and 28-17 map wins) behind a dominant Satanic. Spirit stabilized with 2:0/2:1 wins over weaker upper-bracket opposition and have big-stage pedigree, giving them a clear but modest puncher's chance. I rate VISION ~67% to take the rematch, slightly above the 1.55 line which gives a small edge; the near-fair +1.5 (only fails on a Spirit sweep) is a thin supplemental value at 1.17.

TY enters with a substantial Elo advantage (~84 points, #5 vs #26 globally) and a dominant pre-event form (10-2 series), but their TI run has been uneven (4-3, including losses to Liquid, Aurora, and Iron Wing). NGX has been the surprise package of TI (5-1 series, 10-3 maps), with a 5-series win streak culminating in a reverse sweep of defending champions Falcons, and benefits from a strong underdog narrative with SumaiL's potential farewell. NGX's style is dramatically slower (52min avg vs 42min), favoring prolonged engagements. TY's map-record at TI (11-8) is solid but less dominant than NGX's (10-3). Drafting overlap is significant (Mirana, NP, Clockwerk, Necrophos) and both teams ban heavily against each other's pools. Side advantage is split: TY is much stronger on Radiant (75%) while NGX is stronger on Dire (86%). Combining TY's overall quality and depth (46 hero pool) with NGX's hot form and momentum, TY is a moderate favorite. Series likely competitive, with the 2:1 outcome most probable in either direction.

Team Yandex is favored on paper (84 Elo points higher, 10-2 pre-event series record vs 3-9 for NGX), but Nigma Galaxy has been the surprise of TI 2026 with a 5-1 series record and just reverse-swept defending champions Team Falcons. Critically, TY's wins at the event have frequently gone to 3 games (3 of 4 series wins were 2:1), making a TY 2:0 sweep less likely than the market implies. NGX's hot streak, SumaiL's farewell narrative, long-grind style, and TY's tendency to drop maps give value to NGX +1.5 and ML. The market appears to overweight TY's overall strength while undervaluing NGX's in-event momentum.

Team Yandex enters as the higher-Elo side with stronger early-game numbers and one of the deeper hero pools at TI, but Nigma Galaxy has been the tournament's biggest overperformer, winning 5 straight series via long, comeback-style maps and aggressively banning TY's key Treant/Earth Spirit options. This makes TY only a moderate favorite in a very close BO3, with both 2:1 scorelines more likely than any sweep.

Team Yandex has the higher Elo and stronger early-game numbers, so I make them around a 63% series favorite. Nigma's TI form, long-game resilience, and Yandex's lower sweep rate keep the 2-0 score unlikely enough that Nigma +1.5 maps is the clear value side.

Team Yandex's Elo edge (1457 vs 1373) and early-game dominance (+1.0k gold at 10min, 75% radiant win rate, 2-0 over Liquid) make them slight favorites, but Nigma Galaxy's 5-series TI streak, 10-3 map record with 52-minute average wins, and comeback ability from deficits keep this close. Yandex's weak Dire performance (29%) and Nigma's long-game style reduce the chance of a Yandex sweep.

Team Yandex holds the Elo edge (rank #5 vs #26) and a stronger early game, but Nigma Galaxy's TI form (5-1 series, 10-3 maps vs TY's 4-3, 11-8) and five-series streak including a reverse sweep of defending champs Falcons are strong signals. Nigma's 52-minute average game style directly targets Team Yandex's late-game fade (+467 gold @30 overall), while Yandex's own players openly admit instability and poor play despite wins. I price Yandex at roughly 57% per map, giving them about a 60% series win rate — below the ~68% implied by their 1.48 ML.

TY holds a large Elo edge (1457 vs 1373) and elite pre-event form (10-2), but has wobbled at TI (4-3, 11-8 maps, heavy Radiant dependence at 29% Dire win rate) and admits poor form. NGX is the event's hottest surprise (5-1, 10-3 maps, sweeps of Spirit/LGD/VG plus a reverse sweep of defending champion Falcons), with better player-level stats, comfort on both sides, and elite late-game execution despite weak early-game numbers. Net: a near coin flip with a slight TY edge from class, deeper hero pool, and better ban targeting (Largo/Ember vs NGX's inefficient ES/Treant bans). TY's series historically go three maps while NGX tends to sweep, so I weight 2:1/1:2 outcomes heavily.

Team Yandex holds the Elo edge (1457 vs 1373) and far better pre-event form, but at this TI Nigma has been the sharper side (5W-1L, 10-3 maps, wins over Falcons and Spirit) while Yandex is 4W-3L with losses to Aurora, Iron Wing and Liquid, and its players openly admit poor form. Yandex's severe side split (29% on Dire vs Nigma's 86%) plus Nigma's late-game grind/comeback profile and zero-pressure psychology offset Yandex's faster starts and snowball potential, so I make Yandex only a ~57% series favorite with Nigma very likely to take a map.

Team Yandex holds the quality edge: +84 Elo (rank #5 vs #26), dominant laning (+1.4k gold @20min average) and a 2-0 sweep of Liquid in the UB quarters. However, Nigma arrive on a 5-series win streak including a reverse-sweep of defending champions Falcons, and their profile (negative early gold, 8 grind wins >45min, comeback-heavy) matches well against a Yandex side whose losses show severe late-game collapses (-8.9k @30min in defeats). Side splits matter: Yandex win 75% on Radiant but only 29% on Dire, while Nigma are strong on both (86% Dire), so Nigma should reliably claim at least one map when they control side choice, making a TY sweep harder and pushing the distribution toward 2:1 outcomes. Yandex's shaky group stage (three 1-2 losses) and self-admitted instability temper the Elo gap, but their ceiling and structural early-game edge make them moderate favorites in a series most likely to go three maps.

Yandex owns a significant Elo edge (#5 vs #26) and better pre-event series form, but Nigma's undefeated 5-series TI streak and 10-3 map record at the event indicate peak performance. Yandex favors faster closes while Nigma excels in long grinds and comebacks, making a closely fought BO3 with slight Yandex advantage and likely map exchange.

Yandex's higher Elo (1457 vs 1373) and deeper hero pool suggest slight edge, but Nigma's 5-1 TI series run and strong Dire winrate (86%) with late-game scaling make them dangerous. Independent per-map win prob for Yandex ~0.55 yields expected BO3 split; odds on Nigma ML and +1.5 are generously priced.

Team Yandex holds a meaningful Elo edge (~84 pts) and superior pre-event form (10-2 vs 3-9), plus a wider hero pool (46 vs 31). However, Nigma Galaxy's TI campaign has been exceptional (5-1 series, 10-3 maps, five straight wins including a reverse sweep of Falcons), and they play with zero pressure under KuroKy. Yandex's dire-side win rate is a glaring vulnerability (29%), while Nigma wins 86% on Dire. Nigma's late-game grinding style (52-min avg, 1.8 Roshans/game, 8 wins over 45 min) could exploit Yandex's tendency to fade when trailing. Draft ban pressure is significant on both sides—Nigma targets Earth Spirit/Snapfire, Yandex targets Largo. Overall Yandex is a moderate favourite but Nigma's momentum, mental freedom, and side-strength make this highly competitive.

Team Yandex holds a clear Elo and pre-event form advantage (1457 vs 1373, 10-2 vs 3-9), but Nigma Galaxy's TI run has been extraordinary (5-1, beating Falcons, Spirit, VG, LGD) with a grinding late-game style (52 min avg, 8 wins >45 min) that could exploit Yandex's gold fade after 20 minutes. Yandex's Dire-side weakness (29% WR) and self-admitted instability are concerns, while Nigma's 86% Dire WR and zero-pressure mindset give them an edge in prolonged series. I estimate Yandex ~63% to win the series but only ~22% to sweep 2-0, making the Nigma +1.5 line significantly mispriced.

Yandex has the stronger long-run baseline, with the higher Elo, top-five ranking, strong pre-event form, and better early-game profile. Nigma’s immediate TI evidence is stronger, however: a 5-1 series run, 10-3 map record, five-series streak, and a more coherent late-game and objective-oriented style. With equal rest and no head-to-head history, I make Nigma a narrow favorite in a likely close BO3.

Team Yandex retain a modest edge from their higher Elo, stronger pre-event form, early-game metrics and 2-0 win over Liquid. Nigma Galaxy’s 5-1 TI run, 10-3 map record, wins over Spirit and Falcons, long-game resilience and low-pressure psychology narrow the gap, making a close series more likely than a Yandex sweep. I estimate Yandex at 0.58 to win the series, with Nigma’s map coverage offering the clearest value.

Team Yandex retains a modest edge from its rating, markedly stronger pre-event form, early/mid-game advantage, and greater flex depth. Nigma Galaxy's 5-1 TI record, 6-1 Dire split, late-game conversion, and comeback resilience make the recent form gap substantial, so an upset and a three-map series remain very live.

Yandex's higher Elo, 10-2 pre-event series form, and broader 46-hero event pool keep it narrowly ahead. Nigma's 5-1 TI record, win over Falcons, 6-1 Dire record, and late-game-heavy wins are substantial counterweights, while Yandex's 2-5 Dire record lowers its sweep outlook. The matchup projects as a competitive BO3 rather than a clear Yandex rout.

Team Yandex have a narrow edge from the Elo advantage, dominant pre-event form, stronger early-game differentials, and broader draft flexibility. Nigma Galaxy's 5-1 TI run, win over Falcons, strong results on both sides, and long-game resilience make this highly competitive; Yandex's poor recovery rate when behind is the main risk. A three-map series is slightly more likely than a sweep.

Team Yandex retain a modest series edge from the Elo gap, stronger pre-event form, broader draft pool and superior early-game differentials. Nigma Galaxy's 10-3 TI map run, strong results on both sides and proven late-game resilience make a sweep unlikely and give them a meaningful upset chance.

Team Yandex holds higher Elo (1457 vs 1373) and stronger pre-event form (10-2 series), with solid TI results including 2-0 vs Liquid; Nigma's hot streak (5-1 at TI, SumaiL factor) and low expectations add competitiveness, but Yandex's faster style and hero pool edge make them clear favorites in BO3. Estimated series split reflects this with slight adjustment for Nigma's momentum.

Team Yandex holds higher Elo rating and pre-TI form while Nigma Galaxy shows stronger recent TI results plus SumaiL's presence and lower expectations. Draft overlaps on Nature's Prophet and other heroes create close matchup potential; Yandex slight series favorite at ~55% but with notable upset chance for Nigma.

Team Yandex enters with superior Elo (#5 globally) and strong early-game control (+1433 gold at 20m), demonstrated in their decisive 2-0 quarterfinal sweep of Liquid. However, Nigma Galaxy is on a 5-series surge at this TI (10-3 maps) with exceptional late-game resilience and teamfighting (avg game time 52 min), notably upsetting Falcons. Yandex holds a slight baseline edge, but Nigma's hot form makes a competitive 3-map series likely.

While Team Yandex holds a higher Elo ranking and swept Liquid in the previous round, Nigma Galaxy is on a 5-series win streak at TI including dominant victories over Team Spirit and defending champions Team Falcons. Nigma's exceptional late-game execution (8 wins >45 min) and deep hero flexibility give them a far higher chance of contesting and winning the series than the market odds suggest.

Elo (1457 vs 1373, ~62% baseline) favors Yandex, but the matchup dynamics compress the gap: Nigma is 5-1 at TI with wins over Spirit and Falcons and thrives in long games (8 wins >45min), while Yandex is inconsistent (3 series losses, self-admitted draft confusion) and heavily Radiant-dependent (75% Radiant vs 29% Dire) against a Nigma side that wins 86% on Dire. Yandex's strong early game (+1.4k @20min) meets Nigma's chronic slow starts (-1.1k @20min), so Yandex should lead often, but Nigma's comeback record and superior late-game closing keep them live in every map. I rate Yandex a modest ~57% series favorite, well below the market's 67.6% implied, making Nigma-side prices valuable; sweeps are unlikely given the side-selection split, so the 2:1/1:2 branches carry extra mass.

Nigma Galaxy has dominated TI 2026 (5W-1L series) with mostly 2-0 wins over quality opponents (OG, LGD, Vici, Team Spirit, Falcons). Team Yandex is more volatile at 4-3, including a 1-2 stretch vs Liquid/Aurora/Iron Wing, though they won their last 2-0 vs Team Liquid. Nigma's stable roster (SumaiL/lorenof/Davai/OmaR/GH since June 8) and stronger form give them the edge, with sweeps more likely given how dominant they've been.

Near coin-flip UB semi. Nigma Galaxy has the better tournament resume (5W-1L, 10-3 maps, sweeps of OG/LGD/Vici/Spirit) and showed resilience coming back from a 0-1 deficit to beat Falcons, but they also got blown out 25-8 in that opener. Team Yandex enters on the hottest form: back-to-back series wins (LGD 2-1, then a 2-0 sweep of a top-tier Liquid in the UB QF) built around a unique core-Io strategy opponents feel forced to ban, with a dominant 38-13 map-2 stomp showing a high ceiling. No H2H at TI, similar strength of schedule. I give Yandex a slight momentum edge (~52.5% per-map), which yields a fairly flat BO3 score distribution, slightly favored to go Yandex's way with a strong chance Nigma covers +1.5 (i.e., series reaches three maps or Nigma wins).

Team Yandex arrive off the most impressive playoff-round result — a clean 2:0 sweep of #2 Swiss seed Team Liquid, including a 38-minute stomp — and carry season-long pedigree as 2026 winners of PGL Wallachia S7 and BLAST Slam VII. Nigma Galaxy counter with the best overall TI form: five straight series wins and a 10-1 map record since their opening loss, including a 2:0 over Team Spirit and a 2:1 over Falcons, plus the higher Swiss seed (3rd vs 11th). Yandex's deeper roster, harder bracket path (all their losses were close 1:2s, never swept) and current peak give them a modest edge in what projects as a competitive three-game series.

Nigma Galaxy has been the more consistent team at TI 2026 (5W-1L, 10-3 in maps, four 2:0 sweeps incl. Team Spirit, plus a resilient 2:1 QF win over Falcons), while Team Yandex (4W-3L, 11-8) is never-swept but grindy — all three losses were 1:2s — and arrives hot after sweeping Liquid with arima- in peak form. No H2H; common opponents (LGD, Iron Wing) slightly favor Nigma, and Nigma's core heroes (Necrophos 58% WR) fit the patch better than Yandex's frequent Hoodwink (44%). I give Nigma a slim series edge (~54%), with a three-map grind the most likely outcome since Yandex reliably takes maps off top teams.

Nigma Galaxy is the stronger side: 5-1 in series (10-3 maps) with a five-series win streak including 2:0 over Team Spirit and 2:1 over Team Falcons, playing clean meta drafts (Mirana/Windranger/Necrophos/NP) with a stable five-man roster featuring gh. Team Yandex is 4-3 with all losses a competitive 1:2 and a strong 2:0 over Team Liquid in round 1 powered by arima-'s carry Io/Windranger, but their overall opposition quality and consistency trail Nigma's. Common-opponent signals (LGD 2:0 vs 2:1) also favor Nigma. I rate Nigma ~67% to take the series, with Yandex's live-upset path mostly a 2:1 rather than a sweep.

Nigma Galaxy enter the upper-bracket semis on a 5-1 run with four 2-0 sweeps over elite sides (LGD, Spirit, Vici, OG) plus a 2-1 over Falcons, a tournament map win rate near 77%. Team Yandex are 4-3 with a 3-series win streak capped by a 2-0 over Liquid, but they dropped group losses to Liquid and Aurora. There is no head-to-head history at this event. Nigma's dominant sweeps of top teams and superior form make them the clear favorite; Yandex's recent momentum keeps them competitive but a tier below, so I favor Nigma at ~0.65 series (Yandex per-map ~0.40).

Nigma Galaxy entered playoffs as one of the strongest teams: 4-1 group stage with an 8-2 game record (80% game win rate, second only to Team Vision), a 2:0 win over Team Spirit and a 2:1 upper-bracket win over Team Falcons. Team Yandex went 2-3 in groups, needed an elimination-round win over LGD, and while their 2:0 upset of Liquid shows genuine playoff form, common-opponent evidence (Iron Wing swept Nigma but beat Yandex 2:1; Nigma 2:0'd the same LGD Yandex needed 3 games against) favors Nigma. Both teams contest Windranger/Mirana/NP-style drafts. Nigma is the favorite, but Yandex take maps in nearly every series, so 2:1 outcomes are likely for either side.

Nigma enters on a 5-1 tournament run and a 10-3 map record, including four 2-0 wins, while also adapting well after dropping the first map to Falcons. Yandex is only 4-3 overall but has strong momentum from a convincing 2-0 over Liquid, with flexible Io, Hoodwink and Windranger drafts and a more established current lineup. With no tournament head-to-head, Nigma gets a narrow edge, but the series should remain competitive.

Yandex’s fresh 2-0 over Liquid and stronger season pedigree make it a narrow favorite despite its uneven 2-3 group stage. Nigma has the better TI record (5-1, including wins over Spirit and Falcons) and effective Nature’s Prophet/Bounty Hunter/Mirana structures, but Yandex’s flexible Io/Hoodwink drafts and demonstrated willingness to ban Prophet provide counterplay. With no tournament H2H and both teams carrying strong recent form, a three-map series is highly plausible.

Team Yandex shows solid recent form (4-3 in recent TI series, strong W 2:0 vs TL), with a stable core roster of watson, CHIRA_JUNIOR, DM, Saksa, Malady post-2025 acquisitions. Nigma Galaxy has excellent recent streak (5-1, including W 2:1 vs Falcons and multiple 2:0s) but more inconsistent rosters with frequent changes and stand-ins (e.g., lorenof, Davai, SumaiL returns). No H2H. TI meta favors supports/initiators (HW 61% pick/win, ES 67%, WW 53%, WR 54%, DW 54%). Yandex's recent TL series suggest adaptability; Nigma's power in recent games but TI experience edges Yandex slightly in draft fit. Estimated 55% win prob for Yandex in BO3.

Nigma Galaxy enter the Upper Bracket Semifinals on a red-hot five-series winning streak at TI 2026, including convincing victories over Team Spirit (2-0) and Team Falcons (2-1), propelled by versatile drafts and sharp late-game execution from SumaiL and lorenof. Team Yandex possess championship pedigree from their 2026 Tier 1 titles and rebounded from a shaky group stage with a dominant 2-0 sweep over Team Liquid behind watson's carry play. This clash is projected to be extremely competitive, with Nigma holding a marginal edge due to peak tournament momentum.

Nigma Galaxy has the cleaner TI run at 10-3 in maps, including wins over Spirit and Falcons, but Team Yandex faced the tougher Swiss schedule and has since beaten LGD before sweeping Liquid. Yandex's stronger 2026 title pedigree and flexible Io/Nature's Prophet drafts narrowly offset Nigma's hotter form; with full rosters and no tournament H2H, this is close to a coin flip.

Team Yandex are justified favorites after sweeping Team Liquid 2-0 in the UB QF and the market prices them around 1.48. But Nigma Galaxy have won five straight series with a dominant 10-3 map record and bounced back from 0-1 down to beat Falcons, making them a live underdog. I see Yandex winning ~63% of series, with Nigma's +1.5 map handicap (covering any single map win) as the clearest edge over its 63.3% implied probability.

Yandex's season pedigree (PGL Wallachia S7 + BLAST Slam VII titles) drives the market's ~65% line, but at this event their form is shakier (2-3 groups, 11-9 maps, elimination-round escape) while Nigma is 5-1 with a 10-3 map record including a 2:0 over Spirit and 2:1 over Falcons. Nigma's June-formed roster means season data understates their current level, so I blend to ~58/42 for Yandex. Yandex has never been swept at TI (all losses 1:2), so I shift losing mass from 0:2 to 1:2. This makes Nigma ML (2.70) and Nigma +1.5 (1.58) the value sides, while Yandex ML and -1.5 offer no edge at my probabilities.

Both teams arrive at UB SF in form: Team Yandex (4W-3L) just swept Team Liquid 2-0, while Nigma Galaxy (5W-1L) came back to beat Team Falcons 2-1 (a tougher opponent). Nigma's tournament run has been more dominant (four straight 2-0s mid-event vs OG/LGD/VG/Spirit) and they've lost only once, to Iron Wing in the first series. Both rosters had late stand-in swaps (Yi Zaha in for TY pos5, 1131 + pro100tasher for Nigma) but Nigma's new core already cleared the Falcons test. TY has been scrappier—3 of 4 wins went 2-1 and three losses were 1-2—so I expect a tight, likely 3-map series. I rate TY ~55% / Nigma ~45%, giving Nigma clear value vs the market's ~67/33 split and strong value on the +1.5 handicap (covers any non-2-0 TY win).

Yandex carry more pre-tournament pedigree (Saksa/watson, two 2026 titles) and are priced as clear ML favorites, but Nigma's actual TI form is stronger (5-1, sweeps of LGD/Spirit/Vici/OG plus a 2:1 over Falcons). I rate the matchup near-even with a slight Yandex edge, so the market overprices Yandex and underprices Nigma — creating value on Nigma ML and Nigma +1.5.

Team Yandex is the higher-class side (world #2 by Strafe, $1M earned, BLAST Slam winner) and swept Liquid in the UB quarterfinals, but their TI2026 run has been shaky (4-3, five of seven series going to three maps, losses to Liquid/Aurora/Iron Wing). Nigma Galaxy is the hottest team at the event: 5-1 with clean sweeps of Spirit, LGD, Vici and OG plus a win over Falcons, their only loss to Iron Wing. That form edge is bigger than the market (~65-67% Yandex implied) credits; I see this closer to a coin-flip leaning slightly Yandex on class, which makes Nigma's outright price and +1.5 map line valuable.

Yandex shows strong form (4W-3L in last 7 TI 2026 series, including recent 2:0 over TL), while Nigma is solid (5W-1L) but dropped a map to Iron Wing. No H2H, but Yandex has better recent momentum and roster stability (watson, CHIRA_JUNIOR, DM, Saksa, Malady). Nigma's roster (SumaiL, lorenof, Davai, OmaR, GH) is veteran but less consistent lately. Patch 7.41e favors versatile picks like Hoodwink/Mirana (high meta). Yandex favored in BO3 per recent results and form.

Team Yandex enters as nominal favorites backed by their earlier 2026 Tier 1 titles and a convincing 2:0 quarterfinal win over Liquid. However, Nigma Galaxy is playing peak Dota at TI 2026 on a 5-series win streak with dominant victories over Team Spirit (2:0) and Team Falcons (2:1). Additionally, Nigma's disciplined first-phase Io ban directly removes Yandex's primary draft flex, making this contest far closer than bookmaker odds imply.

Nigma topped the Swiss at 4-1 (10-3 maps; only loss 0-2 to Iron Wing) and then beat Spirit 2-0 and Falcons 2-1, while Yandex went 2-3 in Swiss and needed the elimination round before peaking with a dominant 2-0 over Liquid in the QF. Yandex is a justified favorite on recent peak form (arima- carry Windranger/Io/Lina), but the 1.48 price implies ~68% series equity, which overshoots my independent ~62% read given Nigma's stronger overall tournament body of work and pro100tasher's NP macro game. Value therefore sits on the Nigma side, primarily the +1.5 maps line.

Yandex is the higher-rated side (#1-3 world, Watson/Saksa) and swept Liquid 2:0 in their playoff opener, but they were shaky in groups (3-3, nearly eliminated) while Nigma is the form team of TI 2026: five straight series wins including 2:0 over Spirit and 2:1 over Falcons (11-3 map run). I rate Yandex only a modest favorite (~58%) versus the market's ~65%, so Nigma ML at 2.70 and Nigma +1.5 at 1.58 both carry value; Yandex ML and -1.5 do not clear their implied thresholds.

Nigma Galaxy’s 4-1 group-stage record, 5-1 overall series form, and wins over LGD and Team Spirit show a more consistent tournament level than Yandex’s 4-3 run. Yandex still gets a narrow edge from its stronger long-term roster profile and fresh 2-0 sweep of Liquid, while both teams have flexible drafts around Windranger, Mirana, Ember Spirit and teamfight supports. I expect a close series, making Nigma’s protection against a sweep attractive.

Nigma went 4-1 with an 8-2 map record in Swiss play and followed it by recovering to beat Falcons, making this much closer than season-long reputation suggests. Yandex's stable elite core and fresh 2-0 revenge sweep of Liquid retain a slight edge, but Nigma's adaptable Necrophos, Nature's Prophet and Mirana-based looks should make a sweep unlikely; there is no tournament head-to-head.

Team Yandex remain the favorite because of their stronger established roster, two premier-event titles in 2026, and convincing 2:0 playoff win over Liquid. However, Nigma are 10-3 in maps at TI, have beaten Spirit and Falcons, and retain strong alternatives when Nature's Prophet is banned. With Io and Nature's Prophet likely drawing priority bans, the matchup looks closer and less sweep-prone than the prices imply.

Very tight matchup. Liquid holds a marginal Elo edge (1439 vs 1429) and slightly better pre-event form (9-3 vs 8-4), plus they enter with momentum after eliminating defending champs Falcons 2-1 yesterday, while Spirit dropped 1-2 to TEAM VISION. At TI their records are nearly identical (Liquid 5-2, Spirit 5-3). Spirit won the most recent direct meeting 2-1 on Aug 14, but that was a competitive series. Liquid has stronger results on contested picks (Hoodwink, Windranger) while Spirit is deeper in hero pool (44 vs 36). Composure and the slightly better early-game comeback profile favor Liquid, giving them a narrow edge in what should be a closely contested BO3.

Close matchup between two similarly-ranked teams (Spirit #9, Liquid #6 Elo, separated by ~10 points). Spirit holds a slight H2H edge (3-2 all-time, 2-1 at this TI on Aug 14) but Liquid enters with stronger momentum after eliminating defending champions Falcons 2-1, while Spirit just dropped 1-2 to VISION. Both teams have equal rest (0d) and similar TI series records (5W-3L vs 5W-2L). Liquid tends to win 2:1 when they win (4 of 4 shown TI wins), while Spirit has more score variety. My fair line is Spirit ~52% / Liquid ~48%, making the market's 1.62 on Spirit slightly short. Liquid +1.5 maps is the strongest value as it covers three of four likely scorelines given the projected closeness.

Liquid enter with the higher Elo, stronger pre-event form, and a recent elimination win over Falcons, but Spirit won the TI H2H 2-1 and is similarly rested. This is a close BO3 with a slight Liquid edge overall; Spirit's path is more likely via a 2:1 than a sweep, while Liquid's chances are split between a narrow win and a clearer 2:0.

Team Spirit merits a narrow series edge from the TI H2H win and their slower, comeback-oriented play, while Liquid's stronger phase stats and elimination-round form keep the series close. I model Spirit as roughly a 55% map favorite, which gives about a 57.5% series win but only a ~30% sweep chance; the clearest value is therefore on Liquid covering +1.5 maps.

Elo is nearly level (Liquid +10) and both teams are 11-8 on maps at this TI. Spirit won the earlier head-to-head 2-1, but Liquid has stronger recent momentum and better event draft edges in contested heroes such as Hoodwink and Windranger. I treat it as a near coin-flip with a small Liquid edge, using roughly a 49% per-map win chance for Spirit.

Near coin-flip elimination BO3: Liquid hold a slim Elo edge (1439 vs 1429), better pre-TI form (Falcons 3-0 final) and just eliminated the defending champs, while Spirit won the event H2H 2:1, own the H2H 3-2, and show better comeback resilience (3/8 vs 1/6 from 2k+ deficits). Both are 11-8 in maps at TI with heavy 3-map tendencies (Liquid 5 of 7 series went the distance), so I lean slightly Spirit (~51%) with an elevated decider probability. Drafts are largely a wash: Earth Spirit will be contested/banned, Liquid's Undying/Doom bans clip Spirit flex picks while Spirit's KotL/Treant bans touch Liquid supports.

My read is a near coin-flip with only a slight Spirit edge (~54%): Spirit won both recent H2H series 2-1, has the deeper hero pool (44 vs 36 unique heroes) and better comeback profile (3/8 vs 1/6 when trailing 2k+), but Liquid holds the Elo edge (1439 vs 1429), better pre-event form (1win Essence title, 3-0 over Falcons), just eliminated the defending champions, and Nisha/m1CKe are in strong form while Spirit has shown 0-2 collapses vs VISION and Nigma. The market's ~62% implied for Spirit looks several points too high, so Liquid's ML at 2.35 and Liquid +1.5 at 1.45 both carry positive expected value; Spirit 2:0 sweeps look unlikely given Spirit's wins vs elite teams have mostly been 2:1 and Liquid has taken maps in nearly every TI series.

Near coin-flip between two evenly matched teams (Elo 1429 vs 1439). Spirit hold the event H2H edge (2:1 on Aug 14) and 3W-2L in recent H2H, but Liquid arrive with stronger momentum after eliminating defending champions Falcons 2-1, while Spirit dropped a 1-2 to top contender TEAM VISION. Both teams play long games (44-46 min avg) and their TI series skew heavily to three maps — 5 of Liquid's 6 series went the distance, and both show comeback profiles with negative early gold but positive @30min differentials. Draft-wise Liquid's Hoodwink/Windranger flex is a real edge (Spirit's Hoodwink is 0W-3L), while Spirit counter with superior Underlord and Earth Spirit records. Net: a very slight Liquid lean from Elo and current form, with high likelihood the series goes to a deciding map.

This is far closer than the market implies: Liquid hold the higher Elo (#6 vs #9), better pre-event form (9-3 with a fresh title vs Spirit's 8-4), identical 11-8 map records at TI, and arrive off a strong elimination win over defending champions Falcons while Spirit fell to VISION and earlier dropped an ugly 0:2 to Nigma. Spirit's edges — the 2:1 group-stage H2H win eight days ago, Yatoro's peak form, better comeback record (3/8 vs 1/6 when trailing 2k+ @15) and stronger Underlord/Earth Spirit results — roughly cancel Liquid's momentum, superior XP edge (+183/map) and Hoodwink/Windranger flex advantage. Both teams are slow starters who close late, and 5 of Liquid's 6 TI series plus their H2H went to a decider, so a long, scrappy three-map series is the modal outcome; I rate it near a coin flip with only a hair toward Spirit, making Liquid's prices the value side.

Spirit hold a 2-1 H2H win at TI but Liquid own a slightly higher Elo (1439 vs 1429) and eliminated Falcons 2-1 yesterday while Spirit lost to VISION; both on 0 days rest. Assuming per-map win prob for Spirit ~0.48 yields a closely fought series with Liquid marginal favorites.

Team Spirit hold a slight edge from their 2-1 TI win over Liquid and comparable event map records, but Liquid's higher Elo, superior pre-event form and late-game XPM suggest a close BO3. Independent map win prob for Spirit estimated at 0.53, yielding series score distribution without anchoring to market odds.

This is an extremely tight rematch of the Aug 14 group-stage BO3 that Spirit won 2-1. Spirit holds the H2H edge at this event (3-2 in last 5 maps) and the Underlord/Earth Spirit comfort picks, but Liquid carries a slightly higher Elo, superior XPM/GPM edges, a dominant Hoodwink flex (7-3 vs Spirit's 0-3), and momentum from eliminating defending champions Falcons in an elimination game. Both rosters are well-rested equally (0 days, 2 series each). The draft overlap heavily favors Liquid on Hoodwink and Windranger flex, while Spirit edges Underlord. Given the prevalence of 2-1 results for both squads at TI (Spirit 4 of 8, Liquid 4 of 7), I expect another tight three-map series with Spirit as marginal favorites based on the direct H2H and Collapse/Larl peak performance, but Liquid fully capable of reversing the result.

This is an extremely tight rematch of the Aug 14 group-stage series (Spirit won 2-1). Elo gap is only ~10 points favouring Liquid, and both teams enter with identical rest/load. Spirit have the H2H edge at this event and superior TI pedigree under Miposhka, but they've been inconsistent (two 0-2 losses to VISION, one to Nigma). Liquid carry momentum from eliminating defending champs Falcons and boast better aggregate GPM/XPM edges (+49/+183 vs +11/-43). The H2H pattern (both prior meetings went to 3 maps) and comparable skill level suggest a high probability of a deciding game. I estimate Spirit ~53% to win the series, making the market's 61.7% implied on Spirit ML an overprice and Liquid's 42.6% implied an underprice.

Liquid is a narrow favorite from the higher Elo/rank, stronger pre-event record, and its 2-1 elimination win over Falcons, although both teams have identical 11-8 TI map records and Spirit won their recent 2-1 H2H. Equal zero-rest load and Spirit's broader hero pool keep this close; I lean Liquid 52-48, with a third map slightly more likely than a sweep.

Liquid has the slightly stronger Elo, pre-event record, and TI series record, while Spirit's recent 2:1 head-to-head win keeps this close. Equal rest and similar map records point to a competitive BO3 with 2:1 outcomes more likely than either sweep, making Liquid attractive at both underdog prices.

Liquid hold a narrow edge through the higher Elo/rank, stronger pre-event record, and 5-2 TI series record, supported by successful Hoodwink and Windranger flex usage. Spirit's 2-1 event H2H win, broader hero pool, and stronger recovery record when trailing keep this close; identical 11-8 TI map totals and equal rest make three maps slightly more likely than a sweep.

Liquid's slightly higher Elo, stronger pre-event form and 5-2 TI series record are offset by Spirit's 2-1 event head-to-head win, better early gold profile and 44-hero pool. Equal rest, identical 11-8 TI map records and Liquid's 2-1-heavy event results make this a narrow Spirit lean with a third-map bias.

Spirit have a narrow edge from winning the event H2H 2-1, advancing further through the upper bracket, showing better comeback results, and fielding the broader hero pool. Liquid's slightly higher Elo, stronger pre-event form, positive XP profile, and elimination win over Falcons keep the matchup close; with both teams repeatedly playing tight series, three maps is the likeliest outcome.

Spirit has a narrow edge from its 2-1 event H2H win, broader hero pool and stronger comeback record. Liquid's higher Elo, stronger pre-event form and superior aggregate GPM/XPM differentials keep the matchup close, so Spirit is only a modest series favorite.

Team Spirit holds the H2H edge from their 2-1 series win over Liquid on Aug 14 and has strong momentum after sweeping Iron Wing, while Liquid has a slight Elo advantage and better overall TI series record (5-2 vs 5-3). However, contested picks and bans are balanced, with both teams in excellent form and no rest advantage. This LB QF is expected to be competitive with high variance.

Spirit and Liquid are closely matched with similar recent records at TI (both 11-8 maps) and strong pre-event forms. Spirit's H2H win over Liquid 2:1 at the event and recent sweep provide slight edge, but Liquid's better overall Elo and form balance it out. Expected series outcome in BO3 is competitive.

This Lower Bracket Quarterfinal is a dead-heat rematch of the group stage clash won 2-1 by Team Spirit. While Team Liquid carry momentum from eliminating defending champions Falcons and hold a marginal Elo edge, Spirit's championship pedigree in elimination scenarios and solid draft counter-play against Liquid's core pools (particularly around Underlord and Earth Spirit) make this a near 50-50 encounter heavily tilted toward a full three-game series.

Team Spirit and Team Liquid enter this Lower Bracket Quarterfinal evenly matched, with identical 11-8 map records at TI 2026 and a tightly contested 2-1 group stage series previously won by Spirit. While Spirit holds immense late-game teamfight prowess anchored by Yatoro, Liquid's high-tempo early and mid-game aggression led by Nisha gives them significant parity, creating positive expected value on Liquid taking at least one map and on their outright line.

Both teams are closely matched at TI 2026 with similar BO3 records (Spirit 5W-3L, Liquid 5W-2L). Spirit holds a slight H2H edge from their 2-1 group-stage win, but both teams have made roster changes since then. Spirit just dropped a tight 1-2 to tournament frontrunner TEAM VISION yesterday, but showed upside with a 2-0 over Iron Wing prior. Liquid is coming off a confident 2-1 over Team Falcons. Spirit's tournament results show higher variance (more dominant 2-0 wins but also more 0-2 losses to top sides), while Liquid is more consistent at 2-1. The match is essentially a coin flip with a marginal Spirit edge from H2H and a higher BO3 ceiling.

Near-even matchup: Spirit won the direct H2H 2-1 in the group stage (dominating maps on Kez/NP) and showed a higher ceiling (2-0 sweep of Iron Wing, tight 1-2 vs upper-bracket force TEAM VISION), while Liquid recovered from a 0-2 sweep by Yandex with a comeback 2-1 over Falcons. Both sides are inconsistent in deciders, so a 3-map series is the most likely outcome. Meta check favors Spirit's playstyles (Earth Spirit, Kez, SF cores) slightly, giving Spirit a modest edge.

Very evenly matched lower-bracket clash: both teams are 11-8 in maps at TI 2026 and lost their last upper-bracket series to elite opposition (Spirit 1:2 to #1 seed TEAM VISION, Liquid 0:2 to Team Yandex). Spirit holds the direct edge: they beat Liquid 2:1 in the group stage and were cleaner against common opponents (2:0 vs Iron Wing and Aurora, where Liquid needed 2:1 in both). Liquid counters with the higher Swiss seed (#2 vs #4) and elimination-series momentum after a 2:1 over Falcons with two dominant maps, but their losses were heavier (swept by Yandex). Slight lean to Spirit at roughly 55% per map, with both teams' high-variance stomp-prone styles keeping sweep scenarios meaningful.

Very evenly matched LB quarterfinal. Team Spirit (5W-3L, only losing to the two upper-bracket giants TEAM VISION and Nigma) won the only H2H 2:1 over Liquid in groups and posts cleaner 2:0s vs shared opponents (Aurora, Iron Wing), while Liquid (5W-2L) grinds out mostly 2:1 series and just took down Falcons in LB R1 with a dominant decider. Liquid counter-drafted Spirit convincingly in their group-series game 2, and Spirit showed blowout vulnerability (0:2 losses) plus some lineup/standin volatility, so I give Spirit only a slim edge (~0.53) with an unusually high chance the series goes three games.

Spirit hold a slight edge: they won the direct H2H 2:1 in groups (though Liquid's map-2 win was dominant), own a better map differential (13-9 vs 12-9), and their carry 'black reaper' is in huge form (17/2/13 SF, 15/4/15 NP). Spirit's recent losses came against TEAM VISION (UB finalist) and Nigma, while Liquid were swept 0:2 by Yandex before beating Falcons 2:1 in LB R1 with new offlaner K5, who has integrated well. Both teams fit the 7.41e meta. Liquid's series go to a decider ~70% of the time and the H2H was tight, so a 3-map series is likely; Spirit's top-end form makes them a modest favorite, roughly 54/46.

Spirit won this tournament's only head-to-head 2-1 with two emphatic maps (49-23, 38-22 kills) and has cleaner sweeps (Xtreme, Aurora, Iron Wing), showing the higher ceiling and a meta fit around Kez/Earth Spirit. However, Spirit is volatile, having dropped three series including yesterday's 1-2 to in-form TEAM VISION, while Liquid is battle-tested and resilient with four consecutive 2-1 series and yesterday's win over Falcons. Slight edge to Spirit, but the closeness of the H2H and Liquid's grit make a 3-map series very likely.

Both teams are 11-8 in maps, but Spirit faced the tougher schedule, won the tournament H2H 2-1, and swept common opponents Aurora and Iron Wing. Liquid's stronger Swiss placement and recent comeback against Falcons keep this close, while Nisha's Earth Spirit and Liquid's flexible utility drafts fit 7.41e well. Spirit's deeper Yatoro carry pool and favorable direct matchup give them a narrow edge, with a three-map series most likely.

Spirit and Liquid both have solid TI 2026 form (5-3 and 5-2 respectively), but Spirit beat Liquid 2:1 in group stage. Stable Spirit core (Yatoro, Collapse, etc.) with minor roster tweaks gives them the slight edge; meta is open for aggressive drafts. Probabilities favor Spirit winning the series.

Team Spirit holds a slight competitive edge over Team Liquid, having defeated them 2:1 in the group stage at TI 2026 and shown higher peak execution against tournament contenders like TEAM VISION. Liquid has demonstrated high resilience but has frequently been pushed to three games (5 of their 7 series at this event), making another tightly contested 2:1 series the most probable outcome with Spirit favored to advance.

Team Spirit's H2H 2-1 win (2026-08-14) was with their full roster (Yatoro/Larl/Collapse/Not Me/rue). In recent matches, Spirit has been using standins — black reaper replaced Yatoro, and the most recent LB loss to TEAM VISION (1-2) showed additional roster changes with aura zzq and burundickk. Liquid has a stable roster and strong form (5W-2L), just beating Team Falcons 2-1. The market price of 1.62 for Spirit overweights the H2H result; with standins, Liquid is now the better team. Score distribution reflects likely close series (H2H was 2-1) but with Liquid favored.

Spirit hold the only H2H (2:1 on Aug 14) but enter off a 1:2 loss to VISION and have dropped 3 of their last 5, while Liquid are 4-1 in their last 5 and just reverse-swept Falcons. Liquid are rarely swept (their only 0:2 this event was to Yandex) and most of their series go the distance, so a three-map series is the base case. On current form I lean slightly toward Liquid, making Spirit ML (-1.5) too short while Liquid ML and Liquid +1.5 carry value.

Spirit's 2-1 head-to-head win, clean 2-0 over Iron Wing, and 3-2 Swiss record against the toughest opponent slate give them a narrow edge. Liquid's 4-1 Swiss run and recovery versus Falcons keep this close; their frequent three-map series and effective Hoodwink/tempo drafts make a Liquid map more likely than a Spirit sweep.

Spirit are a modest favorite: both teams are 11-8 in TI maps, but Spirit faced the harder schedule, won the tournament H2H 2-1, and have converted priority 7.41e picks such as Kez and Earth Spirit well. Liquid's 4-1 group record, reverse sweep of Falcons, flexible Ace-Boxi-tOfu drafting, and five deciders in seven TI series keep this close. No stand-ins are listed, and another three-map series looks slightly more likely than a Spirit sweep.

Team Spirit had a recent 2:1 H2H win over Liquid at TI2026 and strong recent form (W2:0, W2:1, W2:0 in last 4 series). Lower bracket QF for Spirit (favored). Liquid is strong but Spirit has home/advantage edge and better meta fit (top heroes like Hoodwink 43%WR). Probabilities favor Spirit 2:0/2:1 heavily.

Team Spirit and Team Liquid are closely matched Tier-1 contenders with deep tournament experience. In their group stage clash at TI 2026, Spirit edged out a 2:1 victory across three hard-fought games. Liquid has forced three maps in five of their seven series at the tournament and consistently takes maps against elite opposition, making a 2:0 sweep by Spirit unlikely and creating significant betting value on Team Liquid +1.5 maps.

Direct H2H at TI 2026 favors Team Spirit, who beat Liquid 2:1, dominating kills (38-22, 49-23) in the maps they won while Liquid took one hard-fought game. Both are elite lower-bracket teams and rosters appear intact. Spirit's overall form is mixed (two losses to TEAM VISION, a loss to Nigma) but they remain a top-tier side; Liquid carry recent momentum with a 2:1 win over Falcons but also a 0:2 loss to Yandex. The matchup is close, with a slight edge to Spirit off the H2H and head-to-head map dominance. I model Spirit's per-map win probability at ~0.53, yielding a BO3 slightly tilted toward Spirit.

Spirit and Liquid are statistically near-equals at TI 2026 (identical 11-8 map records; Liquid even had the better group stage at 4-1). Spirit owns the H2H 2:1 and a higher peak behind their red-hot carry, justifying a modest edge, but Liquid's consistency (4-1 in deciding maps, swept only once all event by top-seed Yandex) makes the market's ~62% implied on Spirit too rich. I rate Spirit ~56% to win the series, with a Spirit sweep unlikely (~28%) given Liquid's resilience, so the value sits on Liquid +1.5 and a small Liquid ML.

Team Spirit won this tournament's head-to-head 2:1 (Aug 14), taking both maps they won convincingly (49-23 and 38-22 kills) behind a dominant carry. Spirit's playoff form is solid — a 2:0 sweep of Iron Wing and a 1:2 loss to TEAM VISION, arguably the tournament's best team — while Liquid were swept 0:2 by Team Yandex in the upper bracket and needed three maps to eliminate Falcons. Both teams' series heavily go to deciding maps (Liquid played 3 games in 4 of 7 series), so a 2:1 grind is the modal outcome. I rate Spirit ~58% overall; no value on the moneylines or Spirit -1.5, but Liquid +1.5 looks slightly underpriced given how rarely either side gets swept in close matchups.

Team Spirit gets a narrow edge from the recent 2:1 head-to-head, stronger carry ceiling, and excellent tournament results on high-impact meta picks such as Kez and Earth Spirit. Liquid’s 5-2 tournament record, repeated 2:1 wins, and comeback over Falcons make this a close series with a substantial three-map expectation.

Both teams are coming off elimination wins on Aug 21, but Spirit holds the recent H2H edge (2-1 on Aug 14, won both maps convincingly) and has looked sharper in their clean 2-0s, while Liquid showed inconsistency (0-2 vs Yandex before bouncing back vs Falcons) and tends to go the distance. The Earth Spirit/Kez-heavy meta suits Spirit's carry play. Overall I rate Spirit around 61% to take the BO3; the market's best prices (Spirit ML 1.62, Liquid +1.5 at 1.45) already imply very similar probabilities (~62% and ~69%), so no menu item offers enough of an edge over my independent estimates.

Elo and pre-event form lean slightly Liquid, while Spirit's direct 2:1 group win and TEAM-VISION-level keep it close. Liquid's Hoodwink draft edge (7-3 vs Spirit's 0-3), their elimination win over Falcons, and the coin-flip-level map matchup make the market look too Spirit-heavy; I price Spirit's per-map win around 52%, producing roughly even weighting on Liqud-favoured scores.

Team Spirit gets a narrow edge after winning the only head-to-head 2:1 and posting cleaner wins over common opponents such as Aurora and Iron Wing, though Liquid’s 2:1 win over Falcons and Spirit’s latest loss to VISION keep the matchup close. Both current lineups are represented in the tournament data with no stand-in noted. Spirit’s access to high-performing Kez and Earth Spirit fits the meta, while Liquid’s Hoodwink, Lina and Windranger flexibility should make a map trade likely.

Nigma Galaxy is on a remarkable Cinderella run at TI 2026 (5-2 series, 11-5 maps in the main event) after a poor pre-event stretch. BoomBoys has been mediocre at TI (4-4) but holds a dominant 4-0 H2H record against NGX this year, including two clean 1:0 wins at EWC with NGX's current roster. NGX plays long, drawn-out games (54min avg) while BB plays faster (47min); NGX has swept 4 of 5 event wins 2:0, suggesting decisive victories. H2H and slight Elo edge favor BB slightly, but NGX's current form and momentum under coach KuroKy with SumaiL's resurgent role-swapped carry play is a strong counter-signal. Slight edge to BB due to historical dominance, with meaningful upset potential for NGX.

Nigma Galaxy have been clearly stronger at this TI (11-5 maps, frequent sweeps) and their long-game comeback style is holding up, while BoomBoys have been inconsistent and needed the lower bracket; BoomBoys' 4-0 H2H and slightly higher Elo keep them competitive. That puts Nigma around a 56% map-win probability, i.e. a 59% series win and most likely a three-map series.

Near coin-flip with a slight Nigma lean. BoomBoys hold the higher Elo and a 4-0 H2H edge (all Bo1s from May/July), but those wins came during Nigma's 3-9 pre-event slump; at TI Nigma is 5-2 with 11-5 maps and quality wins over Spirit and Falcons, while BoomBoys sit at 10-10 maps with wins only over Aurora and Iron Wing. Both teams are equally rested, Nigma's drafts are more flexible (34 heroes, multi-player flex picks), and their never-swept profile at the event shifts loss probability toward 1:2. Net: Nigma ~54% series win, with a 2:0 most likely win shape given their four sweeps this event.

Elo is near-even (1373 vs 1396, slight BoomBoys edge) and BoomBoys owns the all-time H2H 4-0, but those were stale BO1s from May/July before Nigma's transformation. At this event Nigma is clearly the hotter team: 11-5 maps with four consecutive 2-0 sweeps (OG, LGD, Vici, Spirit), a 2-1 over Falcons, and a narrow 1-2 loss to Yandex, while BoomBoys sits at 10-10 maps with shaky losses to Aurora and VISION before reverse-sweeping Iron Wing. Both squads are slow-starting, comeback-heavy teams that play long grindy games, so maps should be contested and close, slightly compressing toward 2-1 outcomes. Draft-wise BoomBoys' top bans (Earth Spirit, Shadow Fiend) hit heroes Nigma barely plays, while Nigma can meaningfully target gpk's Lina and Kataomi's Undying, and Nigma's unbeaten Ember Spirit is a contested leverage point. I lean Nigma as a modest favorite on current form and momentum, roughly 55/45, with the most likely single outcome a 2-1 either way.

NGX's strong TI run (5-2 series) contrasts with BB's 4-4 and perfect 2026 H2H (4-0). BB holds slight Elo edge and bans NGX flex (NP, Necro). Estimated NGX map win prob ~0.47, yielding near coin-flip series with BB slight favorite.

Nigma Galaxy's TI form is exceptional (5W-2L, beating Spirit, Falcons, LGD, Vici, OG) despite terrible pre-event results. Their long-grind style (57 min wins) and strong Dire side (88% WR) give them an edge in extended series. BoomBoys are more inconsistent at TI (4W-4L) but experienced and competitive. The 0-4 H2H for Nigma is concerning but all were BO1s in different contexts before Nigma's current TI surge. Both teams are equally fatigued (0 days rest, 2 series in 3 days). Nigma's momentum and peak performance at this event slightly outweigh BoomBoys' deeper experience, but this should be a competitive series with both teams likely taking at least one map.

Nigma's 5-2 TI record (11-5 maps) and stronger comeback/late-game results give them the better current-event profile. BoomBoys retain the higher Elo, better pre-event record, and a 4-0 recent H2H edge; equal rest and meaningful draft overlap keep Nigma only a narrow favorite.

Nigma Galaxy's 11-5 event map record, stronger wins, and repeated success in long games give them a narrow current-form edge. BoomBoys retain meaningful counterweights through the higher Elo, stronger pre-event form, 4-0 historical H2H, and bans that directly pressure Nigma's Nature's Prophet and Necrophos options. With equal rest and substantial evidence on both sides, a close three-map series is the likeliest outcome.

Nigma Galaxy has stronger current form at TI (5-2 series, 11-5 maps with multiple 2-0 wins) compared to BoomBoys (4-4, 10-10 maps). Despite BoomBoys' historical H2H dominance (4-0) and slight Elo edge, NGX's momentum, experience (SumaiL), and recent TI results give them a slight favorite status in this BO3. Drafts are contested but NGX's Necrophos/Ember Spirit flex picks stand out. Expect a close series with NGX winning most often but not sweeping easily.

While Nigma Galaxy has enjoyed an exceptional Cinderella run at TI 2026 (11-5 maps, beating Spirit and Falcons), BoomBoys hold a 4-0 head-to-head record against them this season and possess higher overall Elo and tier-one consistency. BoomBoys are slight favourites in what should be a tightly contested series prone to going the full three maps.

Nigma Galaxy have been the stronger side at this TI (11-5 maps), winning long grind games and showing comeback consistency, while BoomBoys sit around .500 maps and have looked shaky. BoomBoys' Elo/H2H edge is real but mostly from pre-tournament form; I rate NGX as a slight map favorite, giving them value on both the series moneyline and the 2-0 handicap.

BoomBoys enter as slight favorites based on higher Elo, a 4-0 all-time series/map edge over Nigma, and more consistent season-long form. Nigma's Cinderella TI run and comeback-heavy late-game style keep them competitive, but their negative early-game gold/XP differentials and BoomBoys' head-to-head control tilt the matchup toward BoomBoys. Market prices roughly match my independent estimate, so no positive-EV value remains.

BoomBoys bring the higher Elo and a 4-0 H2H edge (all BO1s from May/July when Nigma was in a 3W-9L slump), but at this event the roles are reversed: Nigma is 5W-2L with wins over Spirit, Falcons and LGD, while BoomBoys are 4W-4L with all wins coming against Aurora and Iron Wing. Nigma's dual-core form (SumaiL 759 GPM, lorenof 9.3 KDA) and proven grind-out profile outweigh BoomBoys' season pedigree here, making this near a coin flip with slight Nigma edge (~53%). The market's 1.62 on BoomBoys (~62% implied) looks too heavy on pre-event reputation.

Market prices BoomBoys as a clear favorite off Elo (#19 vs #30) and a 4-0 all-time H2H, but that H2H is stale BO1s from May-July predating Nigma's current form. At TI, Nigma has been the clearly better team: 5-2 series / 11-5 maps with sweeps of OG, LGD, Vici and Spirit plus a 2-1 over Falcons, while BoomBoys is 4-4 / 10-10 with two losses to VISION and a narrow reverse-sweep of Iron Wing. Nigma's 88% Dire win rate and late-game grind style (9 wins >45min) match up well against BoomBoys' negative gold-differential profile and shaky mid-game. Elo gap is only ~22 points, so I rate this near a coin flip with a slight edge to Nigma's event form. That makes Nigma ML at 2.38 (implied 0.42 vs my ~0.53) solid value, and Nigma -1.5 at 5.00 (implied 0.20 vs my ~0.28, given four 2:0 sweeps at the event) a small-stake value play.

Nigma Galaxy's strong TI run (5-2 series, 11-5 maps) offsets lower Elo and prior H2H deficit vs BoomBoys (4-0 BB). Both teams on 0d rest; draft contests slightly favor NGX (Ember Spirit perfect, BB bans Nature's Prophet). Estimated single-map win prob for NGX ~0.53 yields score probs.

Nigma Galaxy enters this LB QF as the stronger TI 2026 side (5-2 series, 11-5 maps) with a Cinderella run including wins over Spirit, Falcons, and LGD, while BoomBoys sits at a middling 4-4 with two losses to TEAM VISION. The 4-0 H2H for BoomBoys is entirely BO1 from earlier events and less relevant in a BO3 elimination context. Nigma's late-game grind style (9 of 11 wins over 45 min) and dominant Dire side (88% WR) suit a multi-game series. BoomBoys holds a small Elo edge (~22 pts) and more experience, keeping this competitive, but Nigma's tournament form and momentum tilt the series in their favour. The market prices BoomBoys as clear favourite (1.62), undervaluing Nigma's superior event performance.

TEAM VISION's ~107-point Elo edge, #1 ranking and 6-0 TI run make them deserved favorites (~65-67% per map, ~72% for the series), but the market overprices dominance: VISION have swept only 2 of 6 series at this event (dropping maps even to Resilience and Falcons), Team Yandex's playoff series consistently go three maps, and TY hold a 3-2 edge in the last five H2H meetings plus a rising form curve (2-0 over Liquid, 2-1 over Nigma). TY's poor comeback profile (1-6 when trailing 2k+ @15) and 44% Dire win rate cap their upset ceiling, but a close, likely three-map series is the most probable shape.

TEAM VISION (PARIVISION) is undefeated at TI 2026 (6-0, 12-4 maps) with Satanic in MVP form and is the consensus #1 of the final eight, but both playoff wins came 2:1 and Yandex has quietly swept Liquid and beaten Nigma (ranked #3/#2) to reach this final, showing elite playoff form. I rate VISION per-map ~0.65, giving ~0.71 series win; that is below the heavy 1.30 ML price, while Yandex +1.5 (needs only to avoid a sweep) and Yandex ML at 4.00 both look undervalued given VISION's pattern of 3-map series.

TEAM VISION is undefeated (6-0, #1 Swiss seed, beat Spirit twice) but every main-event series of theirs went 2-1, while Team Yandex — world #3 and a Wallachia/BLAST SLAM champion — surged late: 2-0 over Liquid and 2-1 over Nigma in the playoffs after 1-2 losses to top seeds in groups. I rate TEAM VISION ~63% per map, which puts the series around 69/31 rather than the ~77/25 the 1.30/4.00 ML implies, and makes a TEAM VISION 2-0 sweep (~40%) less likely than the 1.94 handicap price assumes.

TEAM VISION is undefeated at TI (6-0 series, 13-2 maps) with wins over elite opponents (Team Spirit x2, BoomBoys x2, Falcons) and a perfect 4-0 record in game 3s; Satanic's carry play has been dominant. TEAM VISION is 6-0 at TI 2026 with a tougher schedule (Falcons, Spirit x2), but 4 of 6 series went 2:1 and they were crushed 8-29 in 28 minutes in one of their losses to Spirit, showing fragility. TEAM VISION is the clear favorite: undefeated 6-0 at TI 2026, #1 Swiss seed, with wins over Falcons and Spirit (twice) and Satanic in dominant carry form. TEAM VISION is undefeated (6-0) at TI 2026 and reached the UB final, but its wins skew toward 2:1 (4 of 6 series), never dominant sweeps. TEAM VISION are 6-0 at TI 2026 with two series wins over Team Spirit plus a win over Falcons, closing out both playoff series with dominant deciders (Satanic's Shadow Fiend going 15/2).
