Team Spirit are a modest favorite on the higher Elo, stronger TI map record, positive phase metrics, and a fresh 2:0 win over Liquid, with Miposhka and MiLAN adding coaching stability. BoomBoys remain dangerous because of their recent playoff momentum, comeback resilience, and favorable recent H2H, while equal schedule load and their 2:1 win over Nigma keep the series close.

Team Spirit is favored based on better Elo (1460 vs 1406, +54 advantage), stronger individual players (Yatoro 9.7 KDA/861 GPM vs Kiritych 6.7/763), and superior phase data (Spirit +293 gold @20min vs BoomBoys -790). Spirit 5-3 TI record edges BoomBoys 4-4. Offsetting: BoomBoys has 3-2 all-time H2H edge, both teams are equally fatigued (0d rest, 3 series in 3 days). My model lands Spirit ~63% to win, market implies 67.6% at 1.48, and BB 2.70 matches my 37%. No clear positive-EV plays on the menu.

Team Spirit holds higher Elo rating and stronger pre-event plus tournament form metrics, making them slight favorites (~52% series win probability). BoomBoys show competitive lower-bracket resilience and similar styles but lag in GPM/XP edges and overall rankings.

Both teams are in similar form in the lower bracket. BoomBoys went 4-4 in groups and is 3-1 in lower bracket (2:0 vs Aurora, 2:1 vs Iron Wing, 2:1 vs Nigma). Team Spirit went 5-3 in groups and is 2-1 in lower bracket (2:0 vs Iron Wing, 1:2 vs VISION, 2:0 vs Liquid). Spirit has a slight edge from their better group stage record and more decisive recent 2:0 wins, but BoomBoys is hot with three straight series wins. Both lost to VISION in the lower bracket. Spirit is a moderate favorite, with most series likely going to a third map given how competitive the bracket has been.

Team Spirit has the stronger tournament baseline at 5-3 in series and 11-8 in maps, compared with BoomBoys at 4-4 and 10-11, and Spirit just swept Team Liquid while BoomBoys needed three maps to beat Nigma Galaxy. Spirit’s current roster has repeatedly converted Winter Wyvern/Centaur setups with high-impact NP, TB, PL and SF cores; BoomBoys’ Kez, SF, WW and Centaur pool plus their recent Nigma win gives them a real upset route, but with more volatility. There is no tournament H2H, so I make Spirit a modest favorite, with a small fatigue edge after playing two maps rather than three in the preceding round.

Spirit enters as a moderate favorite: higher Elo, stronger event gold differentials and better individual GPM/KDA, but BoomBoys' long-game resilience, recent lower-bracket survival and 3-2 H2H edge keep the series closer than the market implies. With both teams on zero rest, I estimate Team Spirit around 58% per map and derive exact scores from an independent map model.

Spirit’s 3–2 group finish came against the tournament’s strongest opponent slate and it just swept Liquid; its recent Centaur/Wyvern/Lina structures map cleanly onto the high-priority meta. There is no TI head-to-head, while BoomBoys’ stable five, Naga/Slark scaling and fresh 2–1 over Nigma give it a credible game-three upset route, leaving Spirit only a 0.61 favorite.

Team Spirit’s 5-3 tournament run includes two wins over Team Liquid and a clean 2-0 immediately before this match, while BoomBoys are 4-4 and needed three maps to beat Nigma Galaxy. Both teams use strong meta staples such as Centaur Warrunner and Winter Wyvern, and BoomBoys have dangerous SF, Lifestealer, Naga Siren, and Slark carry options, but Spirit’s recent form and broader draft coherence give them the edge. With no tournament head-to-head, I expect a competitive series but favor Spirit to close it in two maps more often than not.

Team Spirit enter with the stronger main-stage résumé: they swept Team Liquid 2-0 today (including a 29-8 blowout of tournament-best Vision in their UB semifinal map 2) and their only losses at TI came to top-2 seeds Vision and Nigma. BoomBoys counter with lower-bracket momentum after taking down Iron Wing and then Nigma 2-1, but their map profile is shakier with frequent lopsided losses. No direct H2H exists. Modeling BoomBoys at ~37% per map gives Spirit ~69% series probability, slightly above the 66.7% implied by the 1.50 price; no other line shows value.

Team Spirit is the better-rated side and has stronger event map stats, but BoomBoys' 2026 H2H edge and comparable lower-bracket results narrow the gap. A fixed-map model with Spirit at roughly 0.58 per map gives Spirit ~62% and BoomBoys ~38%, leaving slight value on BoomBoys at the available price.

Team Spirit have the stronger Elo, TI map record, economy and carry metrics, so they are the deserved favorite. However, BoomBoys have shown strong lower-bracket resilience, a favorable recent all-time H2H, and comparable long-game endurance; with equal rest, the upset chance remains meaningful. BoomBoys ML is marginally above the 2.70 price's implied probability, while the other lines do not offer value.

Spirit holds a slight edge with higher Elo (1474 vs 1463) and a better TI series record (5-3 vs 4-4), plus Yatoro is in peak individual form. However, Yandex's 5-0 H2H record (all BO1) gives them a mental edge, and their split-push style could disrupt Spirit's teamfight-oriented approach. Yandex shows boom-or-bust tendencies (massive leads in wins, deep deficits in losses), while Spirit plays more consistently. Both teams played Aug 22, so fatigue is similar. Spirit's slight Elo/form edge and the teamfight-favored meta make them marginal favorites, but Yandex's stylistic advantage and H2H history keep this very close.

Elo slightly favors Spirit (1474 vs 1463) and Spirit's TI 2026 series record is marginally better (5-3 vs 4-4), with strong individual form from Yatoro. However, the market price of 1.40 (71.4% implied) significantly overrates Spirit: Team Yandex owns a perfect 5-0 all-time H2H (5 straight maps won, including two EWC 2026 wins just weeks before this tournament), and their pre-event form is superior (10-2 series vs 8-4). TY's split-push/map-control identity (per Puppey) has historically been a bad matchup for Spirit's teamfight style, and TY has shown late-tournament resilience (megacreep comeback vs Liquid, DM's mentality edge). I model Spirit at ~60% to win the series, with TY's win share heavily weighted to 2:1 outcomes. TY ML at 3.10 offers clear positive expected value versus my 40% probability.

Team Yandex enters as a slight favorite given their 5-0 all-time H2H edge, stronger pre-event form, and matchup identity as map-control pioneers; Team Spirit has elite individual play from Yatoro and better comeback metrics, but also more recent series fatigue and ban priorities that TY can exploit. I set Team Yandex's map-win probability around 0.54, making a 2:1/1:2 split most likely and a 2:0 only moderate.

Spirit has the better TI record and carry stats, but the Elo gap is minimal and Yandex won all five recent H2H meetings. TY's early-game economy edges and split-push identity make them a narrow BO3 favorite; Spirit's comeback ability makes 2:1 more likely than a sweep. I therefore rate TY ~53% to win the series and ~26% to sweep, both above the implied probabilities of the listed prices.

Elos are nearly level and both teams are on 0 days rest, but Team Yandex's 5-0 H2H record, stronger early-game numbers, and draft edges give them a modest map-level advantage. Spirit's Yatoro form, lower-bracket momentum, and late-game/objective stats keep this close. Modeling Team Yandex at ~55% per map in a BO3 yields the score probabilities.

Spirit holds a slight Elo edge and Yatoro is in elite form, but Yandex's 5-0 H2H record, stronger early-game economy (+923 vs +205 at 10 min) and comfort support picks make this much closer than the market implies. I estimate Yandex wins about 46% of maps, leaving Spirit a modest series favorite but Yandex clear value at the offered prices.

Near coin-flip with slight Team Yandex lean (~52%). Spirit holds the Elo edge (#4 vs #5) and Yatoro is in record-setting form, but TY is 5-0 in recent H2H (including 2 wins at EWC in July), is fresher (3 vs 4 series in the last 3 days), and posts stronger early-game numbers (+923 gold @10min vs +205). Spirit counters with better event form (5-3 vs 4-4), superior comeback profile (3/8 vs 1/7 when trailing), championship BO3 pedigree, and a meta that Puppey notes favors Spirit's five-man teamfight identity, while Spirit's ban priorities (KotL x15, Largo x14) directly attack TY's split-push signature. Score lines are tight with slight momentum correlation toward 2:0 results.

Elo gap is tiny (1474 vs 1463) and Yandex holds a 5-0 map H2H edge over Spirit this season, so I see this near 50/50 (Spirit ~54% on better current event form, Yatoro's record-breaking form, and a teamfight meta that suits Spirit, offset by Yandex's matchup dominance and match-play edge). The market's ~71% for Spirit looks heavily shaded, making Yandex ML at 3.10 clear value; Yandex 2:0 at 8.00 is a thinner edge given Spirit's tendency to win or lose 2:1/0:2 maps.

Near coin-flip: Elo is essentially even (Spirit +11, rank #4 vs #5). Yandex owns the matchup 5-0 all-time including twice at EWC in July, enters with better pre-event form (10-2), and has the stronger early game (+923 gold @10 vs Spirit's +205) — their split-push style historically punishes Spirit. Counterweights: Spirit has the better TI body of work, arrives on a 3-series win streak while Yandex just lost 1:2 to PARIVISION, Yatoro is in record-setting individual form, and Spirit's elite late-game/comeback profile (+1523 @30, 3 comeback wins from 2k+ deficits) fits the long-game tendencies of both teams (~45 min avg). Net: a marginal Yandex lean from H2H and laning, but a long, tight three-map series is the modal outcome.

Elo is essentially even (TY 1462.6 vs Spirit 1473.7), and TY owns the matchup 5-0 in recent H2H maps including two wins at EWC in July. TY has the stronger early game (+923 gold @10 vs +205) while Spirit is a slow starter that relies on late comebacks, though Yatoro's record-breaking form and Spirit's lower-bracket momentum (2-0 Liquid, 1-0 BoomBoys) plus TY's fresh loss to VISION keep Spirit a modest favorite in my book. The market's ~71% on Spirit badly overweights pedigree and recent momentum; I make Spirit only ~54% to win a long, grindy series between two teams that both average 45+ minute games.

Team Yandex hold a dominant 5-0 all-time series H2H vs Team Spirit and are framed as tournament favourites, but Spirit's slightly higher Elo (#4 vs #5) and stronger recent map win rate at TI suggest a close match. Assigning Yandex a ~51.5% per-map win probability yields a slight series edge.

Despite Team Spirit's slight Elo edge and stronger recent momentum with Yatoro in record form, Team Yandex's perfect 5-0 all-time H2H and split-push meta prowess keep the BO3 competitive; independent assessment gives Yandex ~40% series win, with market underpricing their ML and 2-0 lines.

Team Yandex holds a perfect 5-0 H2H record over Spirit (all BO1s), superior pre-event form (10-2 vs 8-4), and slightly less fatigue (3 vs 4 series in last 3 days). Their split-push meta innovation and early-game gold leads (+923@10, +1370@20) give them a strategic edge. However, Spirit's Yatoro is in extraordinary individual form (TI GPM record, most kills/tower damage), Spirit scales far better into late game (+1523@30 vs +374@30), and their two-TI pedigree and higher tower damage/Roshan control make them dangerous in extended games. The BO3 format gives Spirit more room to adapt compared to the BO1 H2H losses. This is extremely close, with Yandex's H2H dominance and meta edge giving a narrow advantage over Spirit's individual brilliance and scaling.

Team Spirit has the small Elo and TI-record edge, and Yatoro is in exceptional form, but Team Yandex counters with a 5-0 H2H, a stronger pre-event run, a proven split-push/map-control identity, and slightly lighter recent load. This should be a near-even series with a narrow Yandex edge and a high likelihood of reaching a third map.

Spirit's slight Elo edge, stronger current event record, standout carry form and teamfight-oriented meta give it a narrow advantage, but Yandex's 5-0 recent H2H, stronger pre-event run, split-push identity and lighter recent load keep this close; both teams' long-game profiles make a 2:1 result more likely than a sweep. I price Spirit at 0.52 rather than the 0.714 implied by its moneyline.

Spirit's narrow Elo edge, stronger event map rate and Yatoro's standout form make this close, but Yandex's 5-0 recent H2H, superior pre-event form and early-game/map-control indicators give them a slight edge. Both teams are on no rest, so this projects as a tightly contested series with substantial decider potential.

Spirit's slightly higher Elo, stronger stated TI record, reliable Dire results, and Yatoro's exceptional recent form make it a narrow favorite. Yandex's 5-0 recent head-to-head record, stronger early-to-midgame gold and XP profile, and lighter recent series load keep this substantially closer than the prices imply, with contested drafts supporting a frequent three-map outcome.

The teams are closely matched on Elo and TI performance, but Yandex earns a slight edge from its 5-0 recent head-to-head record, stronger pre-event form, and marginally lighter workload. Spirit's stronger late-game recovery profile, objective output, and Yatoro's standout form make a three-map series more likely than a decisive result.

Spirit has a narrow edge from its stronger TI results, late-game conversion and Yatoro's standout form. However, Yandex's 5-0 recent head-to-head record, stronger early-game differentials and slightly lighter workload make the matchup much closer than the market suggests, with a three-map series most likely.

Team Yandex holds a strong 5-0 H2H edge vs Spirit (all-time), with strong TI form including key wins over LGD and Liquid in the split-push meta. Spirit has slight Elo advantage and standout carries but mixed TI record (5-3). Close draft overlap on contested heroes like Undying/Underlord. Slight Yandex edge in series win prob due to H2H and event momentum; scores balanced accordingly.

TY holds strong H2H edge over Spirit (5-0 all-time, 2-0 recently at EWC) and is red-hot at TI with 4-2 series record including wins over Liquid/LGD. Spirit has Yatoro standout but 3-2 at event and historical losses to TY. Near-identical rest/Elo/form makes it close BO3; slight TY edge from meta (split-push) and recent form yields series win prob ~0.55.

Team Yandex holds a commanding 5-0 head-to-head map record against Team Spirit across recent tier-1 encounters, matching well stylistically through map-widening split push strategies. While Team Spirit have found immense lower bracket momentum behind record-setting individual performances from Yatoro, Yandex's draft adaptability and matchup history give them a slight edge in an evenly matched, multi-map series.

While Team Spirit enters with momentum and record-setting individual performances from Yatoro, the market overprices them relative to underlying parity. Team Yandex holds a 5-0 recent head-to-head record over Spirit across 2026, and their split-push map control style poses severe drafting and tactical challenges for Spirit's preferred five-man teamfight setups. At current lines, Yandex presents substantial betting value.

Team Yandex holds a remarkable 5-0 H2H record over Spirit in 2026, including two wins just five weeks ago at EWC, suggesting a persistent strategic and psychological edge. However, Spirit enters with stronger LB momentum (3 consecutive wins including a 2-0 over Liquid), Yatoro in record-breaking individual form, and a late-game phase profile (+1523 gold @30) that can outlast Yandex's early-game style. The meta shift toward teamfight (per Puppey's commentary) also slightly favors Spirit's identity. Both teams are fatigued (0 rest days), but Spirit has played one extra series. Balancing the H2H dominance against Spirit's current form and meta alignment, I give Yandex roughly 37% to win the series—higher than the market's ~32% implied by 3.10 odds.

Team Spirit has a significant pedigree advantage with the Yatoro-Larl-Collapse core (two-time TI winners) and enters with strong recent form, having won their last four series including three 2-0 sweeps (vs Iron Wing, Liquid, BoomBoys). Team Yandex, despite being competitive, sits at 4-4 in the tournament and was upset 1:2 by TEAM VISION in their previous series — notably, every one of Yandex's four losses came by a 1:2 scoreline, suggesting they struggle to close out close series. Spirit's only losses were 0:2 sweeps to VISION and Nigma, but they've since recovered with dominant performances. Spirit's recent form (5-3 vs 4-4) and individual quality give them a moderate edge in this lower bracket final.

Close BO3 between two elite CIS squads, with a slight edge to Team Spirit. Spirit's main-event lower bracket run has been dominant: clean 2:0 wins over Liquid and BoomBoys (4 consecutive maps, including a 27-6 stomp), while Yandex ended Aug 22 with a demoralizing 1:2 loss to TEAM VISION in the UB final, dropping two maps by 35-12 and 38-15 aggregate and playing again within 24 hours. Both teams lost 1:2 to VISION and both 2:0'd Liquid, neutralizing the common-opponent case; Yandex's titles (Wallachia S7, BLAST Slam VII) and quality 2:1 vs Nigma keep this near a coin flip. Spirit's veteran core (Yatoro/Larl/Collapse) with Miposhka coaching and superior momentum tips it ~55/45 in Spirit's favor, with Spirit slightly more likely to 2:0 than Yandex.

Team Yandex enters as a slight favorite: they are world #2 with two tier-1 titles in 2026 (PGL Wallachia S7, BLAST SLAM VII) and have dominated this matchup in 2026, winning all three recent series (2:1 at ESL Birmingham, 2:0 at BLAST SLAM VII, 2:0 at EWC QF in July) for a 6-1 map edge. Both teams lost 1:2 to finalist TEAM VISION this week, and Yandex came through the harder upper-bracket path (2:0 over Liquid, 2:1 over Nigma), while Spirit counters with a hot lower-bracket run (2:0 over Iron Wing, Liquid and BoomBoys on Aug 22) and TI-winning pedigree from its core. That pedigree and momentum keep Spirit close, but Yandex's season-long level and direct H2H edge make them the more likely winner.

Both teams lost only to grand finalist TEAM VISION at the main event, so this is close. Team Spirit gets a slight edge: better main-event form (7-2 maps, two clean lower-bracket sweeps vs Liquid and BoomBoys), deeper playoff pedigree from the Yatoro/Larl/Collapse core and Miposhka coaching, and stronger drafting on the current meta (Winter Wyvern/Centaur/Ember-priority). Team Yandex counters with a 2:1 win over Spirit at ESL One Birmingham 2026, two 2026 LAN titles, an in-form carry, and a 2:1 win over Nigma (who swept Spirit in groups), but their group stage was shakier and 75% of their series go to deciders. Spirit ~56% to win, with three-map series the most likely shape.

Team Spirit enter the lower bracket final in stronger form (dominant 2:0 wins over Liquid and BoomBoys after their UB loss to TEAM VISION), while Team Yandex ground out 2:1 wins over Nigma and Liquid before falling 1:2 to VISION. However, Yandex lead the head-to-head 7-2 including a 2:0 sweep of Spirit at EWC 2026 a month ago, and both teams' TI form is comparable (5W-3L vs 4W-4L), so I make Spirit only a modest ~62% favorite rather than the ~71% the market implies. Yandex's wins tend to be 2:1 (only one 2:0 all event), while Spirit have posted several clean sweeps, shaping the exact-score distribution.

Team Spirit is favored with a 5W-3L record vs Yandex's 4W-4L, plus a 3-series win streak featuring dominant 2:0 wins over Liquid and BoomBoys. Yandex is competitive (6/8 series went to 3 games, just beat Nigma 2:1 and Liquid 2:0) but lost 1:2 to VISION yesterday getting crushed in the last two maps. Comparing common opponents: Spirit clearly better than Iron Wing (2:0 vs Yandex 1:2), Yandex clearly better than Nigma (2:1 vs Spirit 0:2), both swept Liquid. Through VISION, both went 1:2 but Spirit's map was more competitive. Spirit is the rightful favorite, but the 1.40 price overrates them slightly. Market implies Yandex 32.3%; I estimate ~38% given Yandex's tendency to drag series to 3 games and Spirit's two early 0:2 losses to Nigma/VISION showing vulnerability. Yandex ML at 3.10 offers value.

Spirit is a slight favorite on in-tournament form (consecutive 2:0 LB sweeps over Iron Wing, Liquid and BoomBoys with dominant map control) plus TI pedigree (Yatoro/Larl/Collapse), but the gap is far smaller than the ~69% de-vigged market implies: Yandex beat this same Spirit roster 2:1 at EWC in July, won BLAST Slam VII in June, took a clean 44-min map off tournament-favorite TEAM VISION in the UB final, and beat Nigma/Liquid in the playoffs, while Spirit was 0:2'd by both Nigma and VISION in groups. Both teams were similarly blown out by VISION in deciders, so I rate this a competitive BO3 with Spirit ~59%.

Spirit enters the LB final red-hot: three straight 2-0 sweeps (Iron Wing, Liquid, BoomBoys) with dominant scorelines, Yatoro in carry-god form (998 LH NP, 12/1/5 Tiny), and drafts matching the tournament's best heroes (Ember, WW, Slardar, Centaur). Yandex counters with the season H2H edge (2-1 at ESL One Birmingham, a 'crush' in the EWC 2026 QF last month), an upper-bracket-final run, and watson in form — plus they've never been swept at TI (all four losses 1-2). Both lost 1-2 to VISION, and both swept Liquid 2-0, so they grade as near-equals a tier below the grand finalist. I lean Spirit slightly (~54%) on current momentum and cleaner meta drafts, but Yandex's consistency in taking a map makes a 3-map series the modal outcome.

Spirit is in red-hot lower-bracket form (three straight 2:0s over Iron Wing, Liquid, BoomBoys) and gets a slight edge, but the market's 71% implied on Spirit is inflated by brand and streak bias. Yandex is a top-3 world team that reached the UB final (losing only a close 1:2 to grand finalist TEAM VISION), dominates the historical H2H 7-2 including a 2:0 at EWC 2026, and has comparable playoff-level performance. I rate this close to even: Spirit ~57.5% to win the series. Yandex ML at 3.10 and Yandex -1.5 at 8.00 both carry significant positive EV against my probabilities.

Team Spirit enter the Lower Bracket Final in better form (5W-3L) with dominant recent wins, including a 2:0 over Team Liquid on the back of high-economy cores (black reaper's Nature's Prophet/Terrorblade). Team Yandex are 4W-4L; they can take maps (two 2:1 series, a 2:0 over Liquid) but were blown out 12-35 kills by TEAM VISION in their latest match and tend to lose close series 1:2. Both teams lost to VISION, signalling rough parity below the top side, but Spirit's superior carry output and steadier upper-form make them the slight favorite. Expect a series that frequently reaches a third map with Spirit edging it.

Team Spirit enter the Lower Bracket Final on a two-series win streak (2:0 over Team Liquid, 2:0 over BoomBoys) and are the established powerhouse, whereas Team Yandex are 4W-4L and just lost 1:2 to TEAM VISION. There is no head-to-head at this event. Yandex tend to push series to three maps (6 of their 8 went the distance), so a Spirit series win is favored (~0.69) but sweeps are plausible both ways. Market Spirit ML (1.40) and Spirit +1.5 (1.10) offer no value; Yandex -1.5 (8.00) sits marginally above my independent 2:0 estimate (~13.7% vs 12.5% implied).

Both teams fell only to tournament favorite TEAM VISION in the playoffs (Yandex 1:2 in the UB Final hours earlier, Spirit 1:2 in the UB Semi before sweeping Liquid and BoomBoys 2:0). Spirit enter on a 4-map win streak with their cores in explosive form and more rest, while Yandex were crushed in both decider maps vs VISION, have lost game 1 in their last two series, and carry a heavier fatigue load after the 3-map UB final. Yandex's superior season pedigree (two 2026 Tier-1 titles) and deeper UB run keep them close, but Spirit are slight favorites in what should be a tight, likely 3-map series.

Spirit enter in scintillating form with back-to-back 2:0 sweeps (zero maps dropped vs Liquid and BoomBoys), but those were against weaker opposition. The all-time H2H strongly favors Yandex (7-2, including a 2:1 Yandex win at ESL Birmingham in March 2026), Yandex beat Nigma 2:1 who swept Spirit 2:0 in groups, and both teams pushed TEAM VISION to 3 maps. Yandex are a genuine top-3 side, so this is far closer than Spirit's 1.40 (~71%) implies. I make Spirit ~61% and Yandex ~39%, finding clear value on the Yandex moneyline and marginal value on Yandex -1.5.

Team Yandex are 4-4 in TI series but have won five of their last eight maps, including a 2-0 over Liquid and a 2-1 over Nigma; Team Spirit are 5-3 and also recently swept Liquid, though both teams have shown draft volatility in losses to TEAM VISION. There is no tournament H2H, but Yandex won the two recent non-TI meetings 2-0; their strong Kez, Shadow Fiend and Earth Spirit results give them a narrow edge, tempered by Spirit's fresher one-map lower-semifinal win and high carry ceiling.

Team Spirit have the stronger TI baseline and arrive after consecutive 2:0 wins over Team Liquid and BoomBoys, with Winter Wyvern and high-output core drafts converting well. Team Yandex remain dangerous: they beat Spirit 2:0 at the EWC, swept Liquid, and defeated Nigma in this playoff run, so Spirit are only a moderate favorite and Yandex should have a good chance to take a map.

Yandex has the stronger season-long baseline: three major titles, an upper-bracket run here, broad draft flexibility, and a 2-0 win over the current Spirit lineup at EWC 2026. Spirit is hotter at TI, winning four straight maps over Liquid and BoomBoys, while both teams recently lost 1-2 to TEAM VISION. Yandex's flexible Io/Earth Spirit options create extra draft pressure and give them a modest edge in an otherwise close matchup.

Team Yandex is a newly formed CIS squad (acquired Cyber Goose roster mid-2025) with solid local form (4-4 in recent TI series) but no prior elite exposure. Team Spirit, multiple-time TI winner with Yatoro-led core, showed strong upper-bracket results (5-3) and better H2H history vs mid-tier opponents. Lower-bracket final favors Spirit's experience and star power; Yandex's upsets prove they can win maps but lack consistency against top teams. Patch 7.41e and meta (strong supports like Winter Wyvern) align with Spirit's proven heroes.

Team Spirit enters the Lower Bracket Final with immense momentum after sweeping both Team Liquid and BoomBoys 2-0, backed by stellar carry performances from Yatoro and Collapse's offlane control. Team Yandex pushed tournament favorites TEAM VISION to three games in the Upper Bracket Final behind watson and Saksa, but Spirit's championship pedigree and high execution level in elimination matches give them a slight edge.

Spirit has the cleaner TI run and a slight draft edge, with its core trio excelling on 7.41e staples while routinely denying CHIRA_JUNIOR's Earth Spirit. However, Yandex is 5-3 across playoff maps against Liquid, Nigma and Vision, recently swept this Spirit roster at EWC, and has the stronger season-long H2H; with both teams fielding full rosters, Spirit is only a modest favorite.

Team Spirit has superior recent form (5-3 in last 8 series) and experienced roster with Yatoro, while Team Yandex (4-4) is a newer CIS org with stand-in-heavy roster and recent losses. No prior H2H at TI. Lower bracket final is high-variance; Spirit favored overall but series can split easily. Probabilities derived from form, meta fit, and bracket context without odds anchoring.

Team Spirit comes into the Lower Bracket Final with immense lower-bracket momentum following convincing 2:0 sweeps over Team Liquid and BoomBoys, powered by dominant performances from Yatoro and Collapse. Team Yandex dropped to the lower bracket after a hard-fought 1:2 series against TEAM VISION, showcasing high mechanical ceilings through watson and Saksa but occasionally faltering in mid-to-late game macro execution. Spirit holds the upper hand in playoff composure and drafting depth, making them favorites to advance to the Grand Final, though Yandex has enough firepower to secure a map.

Yandex has a narrow edge after 2-0 wins over Spirit at both BLAST Slam VI and EWC, plus TI playoff wins over Liquid and Nigma. Spirit’s better Swiss record and its fresh 2-0 over Liquid keep this close; both teams have broad, effective 7.41e pools, making a three-map series relatively likely.

Spirit enters with Lower Bracket momentum — four straight dominant map wins over Liquid and BoomBoys — and their only playoff loss came against grand-finalist TEAM VISION. But Yandex's path is at least as strong: 2:0 over Liquid, 2:1 over Nigma, and a 1:2 loss to TEAM VISION in the UB Final, with watson in elite carry form. Yandex also beat Spirit 2:1 in their last meeting (March) and was ranked above Spirit in pre-playoff power rankings. I make Spirit roughly a 59% per-map favorite, leaving Yandex ~37% to win the series — better than the 3.10 price implies.

Spirit has the better recent playoff map profile, including a cleaner shared-opponent showing versus TEAM VISION and repeated successful Winter Wyvern/Centaur structures. Yandex still swept Liquid and beat Spirit 2-0 at EWC in July, while its Io-centered draft upside and broader historical matchup edge keep this much closer than the money line suggests. I make Spirit a modest favorite, with a deciding map slightly more likely than either sweep.

overall.unit: one series × configuration; common to all 12 original models

configuration_stability.missing_forecasts: Use all remaining eligible forecasts, as in the configuration leaderboard; do not impute missing answers.
configuration_stability.ties: Every tied leader receives one first place.

configuration_costs.basis: Recorded usage.cost.total for eligible forecasts only; excludes retries, failed runs and separately billed search.

lexicon.source: visible final output.reasoning only; case-insensitive whole-word patterns
lexicon.interpretation: Positive r means the word accompanies larger Brier errors; exploratory associations, not causal effects or held-out prediction.
lexicon.adjustment: Pearson correlation after removing additive match, model and configuration effects from both the word-presence indicator and Brier error
